title: Chairman
clean_text: Message from the Chairman of the Board of Trustees It is my great honor to welcome you to Southeast University (SEU), a renowned private institution for higher education with affordable expenses dedicated to the pursuit of academic excellence, innovation, and social impact. As Chairman of the Board of Trustees, I take immense pride in the strides that our university has made in fostering an environment where students, faculty, and researchers can thrive and make meaningful contributions to both the nation and global landscape. Our university was founded on the principles of integrity, knowledge, and service. We believe in nurturing not only academic excellence but also the values of critical thinking, leadership, and ethical responsibility. We aim to embrace students from both privileged and underprivileged society to prepare them for the challenges of tomorrow in an ever-evolving world. We are committed to provide a world-class education, backed by highly qualified faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, and a dynamic curriculum that holds both tradition and innovation. Our partnerships with industry and international institutions further enhance the learning experience, giving our students access to real-world applications and global perspectives. I invite you to explore all that SEU has to offer. Together, we can continue to build a brighter future for our students, our community, and our nation. title: Chancellor Message from the Pro Vice Chancellor
clean_text:
Chancellor Message from the Pro Vice Chancellor

It is with great pride and enthusiasm that I extend a warm welcome to each of you to Southeast University, one of the fastest-growing and top-ranked private universities in Bangladesh. Nestled in the heart of the Dhaka city center, our university boasts three distinguished schools, along with an institute. From the School of Science and Engineering to the Southeast School of Business, and the School of Arts and Social Sciences, our academic landscape is rich and diverse. Within these schools, we house a total of 10 departments, covering a wide array of disciplines including Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Textile Engineering, Architecture, Pharmacy, Business Administration, Economics, English, Law, and Bangla Language and Literature. With over 12,000 undergraduate and graduate students and a faculty pool of more than 400 experienced members, we're committed to fostering excellence in education.

At Southeast University, we believe that education goes beyond the classroom. We are committed to nurturing talent, fostering creativity, and promoting intellectual growth. Our faculty members are dedicated to staying abreast of the latest developments in their fields through ongoing research and study, ensuring that they impart cutting-edge knowledge and skills to our students. Our goal is to not only prepare students for success in their chosen careers but also to instill in them a sense of responsibility towards society and humanity at large.

Our faculty members are actively engaged in research, regularly publishing in prestigious international journals and conferences. Even at the undergraduate level, our students have the opportunity to participate in research projects alongside their professors, gaining valuable hands-on research experience.

Life at Southeast University is vibrant and dynamic, with a plethora of opportunities for both academic and personal growth. Our 19 clubs cater to a wide range of interests, whether you're passionate about photography, debate, music, robotics, entrepreneurship or beyond. We invite you to take a virtual tour of our university and discover all that Southeast University has to offer.

I look forward to working closely with each of you as we chart a course towards a brighter future.

Prof. M. Mofazzal Hossain, PhD, SM IEEE

title: Sustainable Climate Action Policy
clean_text:
Sustainable Climate Action Policy

Background
Achieving net-zero carbon emissions has become an urgent global priority to mitigate the effects climate change and meet international commitments, such as those outlined in the Paris Agreement. 148 countries have formally committed to carbon neutrality, and all 198 parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) have enacted laws addressing climate action. At COP28, nations agreed to "triple the total renewable energy capacity from 3.5 TW to 11 TW by 2030" and "double annual improvements in energy efficiency from 2% to 4% by 2030". As a responsible institution of higher learning, Southeast University (SEU) is fully committed and embraces these objectives, committing to a 50% reduction campus carbon emissions by 2030, in line with Dubai's ambitious climate action plan. SEU aims to align its environmental and operational strategies with national priorities and the United Nations' sustainability agenda, while supporting the Government of Bangladesh in its climate commitments.

Institutional Commitment to the SDGs
Appoint an SDG Committee under the Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) or Institute of Research and Training to oversee all SDG-related initiatives.
Develop a University Sustainability Plan with goals linked to specific SDGs.
Publish an annual SDG Progress Report showcasing achievements, innovations, and data relevant to the QS Sustainability Rankings.
Establish an SDG Data Management Unit to coordinate data gathering for QS Sustainability Rankings.
Maintain documentation and evidence of initiatives (e.g., event reports, project outcomes, photos, MoUs).
Use standardized templates for reporting in alignment with QS data submission requirements.
Conduct internal reviews and audits of SDG performance indicators annually.
Use feedback mechanisms from stakeholders to improve practices.
Benchmark progress against national and international institutions.
Create dedicated SDG webpage on the Southeast University website.
Regularly update progress through newsletters, publications, and social media.
Celebrate key SDG milestones and global sustainability days.
Conduct workshops and training sessions for faculty, staff, and students on SDG alignment.
Promote participation in global SDG conferences, challenges, and ranking-related webinars.
Encourage student clubs and departments to adopt and promote individual SDGs.

Our Sustainable Climate Action Policy focuses on key SDGs, particularly:
■ SDG 1: No Poverty
■ SDG 3: Good Health & Well-being
■ SDG 4: Quality Education
■ SDG 5: Gender Equality
■ SDG 6: Clean Water
■ SDG Affordable and Clean Energy
■ SDG 8: Decent Work
■ SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure
■ SDG 10: Reduced Inequality
■ SDG 13: Climate Action
■ SDG 17: Partnerships

Objectives
■ To progressively minimize Southeast University's contribution to carbon emissions and strive towards achieving a zero-carbon footprint.
■ To promote sustainable energy use and environmental responsibility in all operations.
■ To foster awareness, participation, and behavioral change among faculty, students, and staff.

POLICY:
1. The Sustainable Climate Action Policy of Southeast University will serve as a strategic guideline to gradually reduce carbon emissions from SEU transport and campus operations.
2. A new green building campus will be constructed for several departments, incorporating sustainability principles and powered primarily through renewable energy. The Planning and Development department will be responsible.
3. Solar panels already installed on the rooftop of existing campus buildings will continue contributing to the campus grid through Main Distribution Boards (MDB). Energy-efficient LED lighting will gradually replace old bulbs and fixtures. The Engineering department will oversee this.
4. Faculty and students will be encouraged to carpool to reduce the number of individual vehicles. Microbus transport will be provided for university staff to reduce the need for private transport. The Transport management office, with support from Student Affairs and HR, will coordinate this initiative.
5. Faculty members will be encouraged to use hybrid vehicles and bicycles where possible. The HR department and Sustainability Committee will oversee this initiative.
6. The use of air conditioners will be minimized where possible, supported by awareness campaigns on energy conservation. All departments will ensure that lights and electrical devices are turned off when not in use to conserve energy. The Office of the information technology (IT) and Engineering Department will coordinate these efforts.
7. The university will continue its transition to paperless operations for internal communication, meetings, and documentation. Additionally, meeting durations will be optimized to minimize energy usage. The office of the information technology (IT) will manage this.
8. Proper waste segregation, recycling, and disposal will be enforced throughout the campus to ensure environmentally responsible waste management. The administrative units will oversee this.
9. The campus will be declared as a "plastic free campus" and regular awareness programs will be arranged by the students' affairs office.
10. Tree plantation programs will be held regularly to improve green coverage and air quality. Open green spaces will be maintained and enhanced to support biodiversity and campus aesthetics. The Sustainability Committee and student clubs will take the lead.
11. Workshops, seminars, and awareness campaigns on environmental sustainability will be organized for the SEU community. Students and faculty will be encouraged to initiate sustainability-focused research and projects. The Office of Institute of Research and Training (IRT) will facilitate this.
12. A dedicated Sustainability Committee will monitor the implementation of this policy and evaluate progress towards carbon reduction. Annual environmental impact reports will be prepared and published to maintain transparency and measure achievements.
13. These policy guidelines will be circulated widely among all stakeholders.
14. Install low-flow faucets and dual-flush toilets across campus.
15. Launch a "Water Watch" campaign to educate students and staff about water-saving habits.
16. Reuse greywater (e.g., from sinks) for gardening or cleaning purposes.
17. Students can map local climate vulnerabilities (e.g. water logging, heat islands) using GIS.
18. Install water-saving technologies and promote native tree planting (i.e., neem, banyan, krishno chura etc.).
19. Establish partnerships with NGOs, industries, and government bodies for SDG-related projects.
20. Business and social welfare club students can co-develop small business models with local women (e.g., tailoring, handicrafts).
21. Southeast Welfare Club students can tutor children in slum areas.
22. CSE, English, and Business Schools can organize weekend skills workshops (digital literacy, English, financial literacy).

This policy reinforces Southeast University's commitment to driving positive change through sustainable practices, education, and outreach. By aligning with the SDGs and QS Sustainability Rankings, SEU seeks to elevate its global reputation while contributing meaningfully to a more sustainable and equitable world.

title: Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy
clean_text:
Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy

1. Purpose
Southeast University (SEU) has put in place procedures that promote an anti-bribery culture inside the organization because it is committed to doing business in an honest and moral manner. The University is dedicated to performing its academic and extracurricular activities on campus or in business relations with outside companies in a professional, equitable, and honest manner. It has a zero-tolerance policy against bribery and corrupt practices. This policy was put in place to guard against corruption and bribery while encouraging honesty, openness, and responsibility across the university.

2. Scope
All members of the SEU community are covered by this policy, including administrators, faculty, officers, employees (permanent, temporary, or fixed-term), consultants, contractors, trainees, casual employees, volunteers, interns, students, agents, sponsors, business partners, and third-party representatives worldwide, as well as any other individual connected to SEU, wherever they may be acting on SEU's behalf.

3. Policy Statement
All forms of corruption and bribery are strictly prohibited under SEU. In order to influence decisions or obtain unfair benefits in academic, administrative, or procurement matters, it is illegal to offer, give, solicit, or accept any form of bribery, including cash, gifts, favors, or services. Examples of prohibited conduct include:
- Offering or accepting money to influence exam results or admissions
- Providing gifts or favors to secure contracts or services
- Using university resources for personal gain or to benefit others improperly

4. Gifts and Hospitality
This policy does not forbid modest gifts or appropriate hospitality, as long as certain guidelines are followed. All staff should adhere strictly to the following guidelines in respect of gifts, hospitality, and entertainment:
- Never offer, promise, or give a gift, hospitality, or entertainment where this may be construed as a bribe or be otherwise improper.
- Never request, agree to, or accept a gift, hospitality, or entertainment where this may be construed as a bribe or be otherwise improper.
- Never offer, promise, or give a gift, hospitality, or entertainment to a public official where this may be construed as a bribe or an attempt to influence the public official in his/her official capacity.
- For gifts, hospitality, and entertainment, staff need to obtain prior approval from the competent authorities before accepting or offering gifts, hospitality, and entertainment of a certain level or involving categories of recipients.

5. Resources & Responsibilities
Adequate resources, including financial, technological, and human resources are allocated to support the implementation of this Policy. A committee is designated for overseeing the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of anti-bribery and anti-corruption initiatives at SEU. The anti-bribery and anti-corruption committee constitution for the Policy is as follows:
- Proctor Chairman
- One Dean Member
- Two Heads of the Departments Members
- Two Professors Members
- One Assistant Proctor (nominated by Proctor) Member Secretary

6. Reporting, Protection & Recording
Southeast university encourages prompt reporting of any suspected bribery or corruption through official channels. Reports may be submitted confidentially to the anti-bribery and anti-corruption committee. Retaliation against whistleblowers will not be tolerated. Detrimental treatment refers to dismissal, disciplinary action, threats, or unfavorable treatment in relation to the concern the individual raised. If anybody has reason to believe that he or she has been subjected to unjust treatment because of a concern or refusal to accept a bribe, the matter should be informed to the Registrar office immediately. The University will keep detailed and accurate financial records and will have appropriate internal controls in place to act as evidence for all payments made. The University will declare and keep a written record of the amount and reason for hospitality or gifts accepted and given, and understand that gifts and acts of hospitality are subject managerial review. Where payments are made to third parties, the legitimate business reason for such payments must always be clearly recorded.

7. Disciplinary Action
Violations of this policy will result in disciplinary measures, including suspension, dismissal, legal action, or contract termination, depending on the severity of the breach. The policy outlines clear disciplinary actions that will be taken against individuals found engaging in bribery or corruption. These measures may include termination of employment or student status, contract termination, and, if necessary, legal action.

8. Review and Implementation
The Policy shall be reviewed periodically to ascertain the effectiveness of the implementation of anti-bribery and anti-corruption practices.

title: Purpose of Introducing This Policy at SEU:
clean_text:
Southeast University (SEU) is committed to integrating the principles of sustainability into all aspects of its institutional operations, particularly within procurement and supply chain activities. SEU is highly conscious of the environmental, social, and economic impacts of purchasing decisions and strives to be a responsible leader aligning its procurement practices with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The university adopts innovative approaches to environmental stewardship, ethical sourcing, and circular economy models. As part of this commitment, SEU has established the Sustainable Procurement Advisory Committee (SPAC) to monitor and evaluate procurement activities in line with sustainability principles.

Purpose of Introducing This Policy at SEU:
1. One of the main goals of introducing this policy is to ensure the procurement and use of products and services that are ethically sourced, environmentally sound, and economically viable over their entire life cycle.
2. To reduce the university's carbon footprint by promoting the procurement of energy-efficient, low-emission, recyclable, and eco-certified products.
3. To avoid suppliers involved in exploitative practices (e.g., child labor, unsafe working conditions, environmental negligence) and promote fair labor standards.
4. To build awareness and capacity among staff, faculty, and suppliers to make informed decisions aligned with sustainable procurement goals.

Scope of Application:
This policy applies to all academic departments, research centers, and administrative departments of Southeast University that are involved in procurement activities. It encompasses both operational and capital purchases, ensuring that all acquisitions align with the university's commitment to sustainability. The scope includes, but is not limited to, the procurement of office stationery, IT equipment, laboratory instruments, furniture, construction materials, food and catering services, and transportation and logistics services. All procurement decisions within these categories must adhere to the principles outlined in this policy to support ethical sourcing, environmental responsibility, and long-term economic value.

Key Principles:
1. Supplier Assessment: Suppliers must be evaluated for compliance with ethical labor practices, environmental responsibility, and fair trade principles. The Sustainable Procurement Advisory Committee (SPAC) may ban suppliers involved in child labor, unsafe working conditions, or environmental violations from participating in university tenders.
2. Preference for Certified Products: Priority will be given to products and services that are certified as eco-friendly (e.g., ENERGY STAR, FSC, ISO 14001, Fair Trade).
3. Life Cycle Cost Analysis: Products should be chosen based on their total cost over time, not just the cheapest price. This includes costs for purchasing, maintenance, energy consumption, use, and disposal.
4. Green Procurement Quotas: Southeast University has set a minimum 50% annual target for procuring sustainable goods (e.g., 50% of all office supplies must be recyclable or biodegradable). SEU is committed to increasing this quota in subsequent years.
5. Digital Procurement Process: Southeast University has developed software to automate the entire procurement process without using paper, integrated into the university management system (UMS). All procurement workflows must utilize this software to follow the process.
6. Energy-Efficient Equipment Only: All new electronic or mechanical equipment purchased must meet or exceed energy efficiency standards.
7. Training & Capacity Building: The Sustainable Procurement Advisory Committee (SPAC) will conduct regular training for procurement staff, faculty, and suppliers on sustainable procurement policies and best practices on a scheduled basis.
8. Monitoring & Reporting: The Sustainable Procurement Advisory Committee (SPAC) will collect data from the procurement department and prepare an annual sustainability procurement report for transparency and improvement.
9. Avoid Non-Biodegradable Items: Southeast University is committed to reducing plastic waste by minimizing the procurement of single-use plastics and other non-biodegradable items. All departments and suppliers should avoid products made from materials that do not decompose naturally, and plastic packaging should be replaced with eco-friendly, biodegradable alternatives whenever possible.
10. Chemical Management: Procurement decisions must minimize the use of substances such as PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), VOCs (volatile organic compounds), and other toxic or non-recyclable materials. Departments and suppliers are encouraged to choose safer, non-toxic, and biodegradable alternatives whenever available to promote a healthier campus and reduce environmental pollution.
11. Waste Minimization: The concerned procurement department will follow the principles of the circular economy, which focus on reducing waste and maximizing resource use. The "4Rs" — Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle — encourage rethinking product design, reducing consumption, reusing materials whenever possible, and recycling what can't be reused.
12. Local Procurement: Source locally where possible to reduce transportation emissions and strengthen local economies.

Sustainable Procurement Process at SEU:
1. Initiation: Purchase Requisition (PR) through UMS from departments must include sustainability considerations (e.g., energy efficiency, recyclability, and environmental impact).
2. Review: Regular consumable items will be reviewed annually by the Sustainable Procurement Advisory Committee (SPAC), and a list of sustainable and environmentally friendly items will be prepared through proper analysis. These items do not need to be re-evaluated repeatedly. Other items will be reviewed by SPAC on a case-by-case basis, and the committee will provide expert opinions accordingly.
3. Defining Specification: Based on expert opinions from SPAC and other relevant committees (if required), the Procurement Office will finalize the specifications of the required items.
4. Vendor Invitation: Suppliers will be invited to submit quotations based on the detailed specifications finalized by the Procurement Office.
5. Evaluation: Bids will be reviewed not just on price and technical compliance but also on environmental certifications, ethical labor practices, waste management strategies, and supplier diversity and inclusion.
6. Awarding Work Order: The Selection Committee will approve vendors who meet both performance and sustainability criteria.
7. Implementation and Monitoring: Contracts will include sustainability clauses, and SEU reserves the right to audit compliance.
8. Reporting: Annual reporting on sustainable procurement metrics (e.g., percentage of green products, vendor diversity) will be published as part of SEU's sustainability report.

title: Scope
clean_text:
Diversity Equality And Inclusion Dei Policy Southeast University (SEU), Dhaka, Bangladesh, is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and diverse academic community that reflects its motto, "Meeting the challenges of Time". Recognizing the value of diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences, SEU strives to create an environment where all individuals - students, faculty, staff, and stakeholders - feel respected, valued, and empowered to contribute to the university's mission. from different institutions of the world adapted to align with SEU's cultural and legal context, including compliance with the Private Universities Act, 2010, and Bangladesh's constitutional principles of equality. The Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion Policy of Southeast University (SEU) is dedicated to cultivating a vibrant and equitable academic community by promoting diversity through embracing individuals from varied backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, religion, socioeconomic status, disability, age, and sexual orientation. It ensures equality by providing fair opportunities and dismantling systemic barriers to participation and success, enabling all members to access education, employment, and resources without discrimination. Furthermore, the policy fosters inclusion by creating a sense of belonging, where every student, faculty, staff, and stakeholder feels respected, valued, and empowered to thrive, contributing to SEU's mission of excellence in education and societal advancement.

Scope
This policy applies to all members of the SEU community, including students, faculty, staff, administrators, visitors, and partners, across all university activities—academic, administrative, and extracurricular—on and off campus.

Definitions
Diversity: The presence of differences within the SEU community, encompassing identities, experiences, and perspectives.
Equality: Ensuring fair treatment, access, and opportunities for all, eliminating discrimination and bias.
Inclusion: Creating an environment where all individuals feel respected, valued, and able to participate fully.

Principles
Drawing from global university policies, SEU's DEI framework is guided by the following principles:
1. Respect for All: Every individual is treated with dignity, free from discrimination, harassment, or prejudice, as emphasized in the University of Toronto's equity policy.
2. Equitable Access: SEU ensures fair access to education, employment, and resources, removing barriers for underrepresented or marginalized groups, inspired by Harvard University's commitment to opportunity.
3. Inclusive Excellence: Diversity is a driver of academic and institutional excellence, as championed by the University of Melbourne, enhancing learning and innovation.
4. Accountability: SEU holds itself accountable for implementing and monitoring DEI goals, aligning with University College London's transparent reporting practices.
5. Cultural Sensitivity: The policy respects Bangladesh's cultural context while promoting global inclusivity standards, ensuring alignment with local laws and values.

Policy Statements
1. Assurance of Diversity
Southeast University recognizes that diversity is a basis for academic distinction and innovation. Southeast University promotes diversity among its students, faculty, and staff by welcoming individuals from different cultural, ethnic, religious, socioeconomic, and geographic backgrounds. SEU's recruitment and admissions policies seek to enable individuals with abilities, regardless of origin, to be enabled to gain access to quality education and employment opportunities. In establishing diversity among the population, SEU enhances learning experience and enables its students to become global players.

2. Encouragement of Equality
Equality is a core value instilled into SEU's policies and practices. The university is committed to making equal opportunities available to all the students and staff, so that no individual will be discriminated against on grounds of gender, race, religion, disability, or economic background. SEU has taken measures to eliminate systemic barriers and achieve equality in academic, administrative, and extracurricular endeavors. For instance, the university offers scholarships and financial aid to underprivileged students so that financial constraints do not hinder access to education. SEU has also established grievance redress systems address any instances of discrimination or inequality in a timely and effective manner.

3. Inclusive Campus Environment
Inclusion is at the heart of SEU's vision of building an inclusive and nurturing environment for everyone in its community. The university has made different initiatives to ensure that its campus is accessible and inclusive for individuals with disabilities. This includes providing ramps, elevators, and other facilities to serve students and staff with physical disabilities. SEU also supports inclusive pedagogies, which help teachers adopt pedagogies that address diverse learning needs and styles. Moreover, the university organizes workshops, seminars, and cultural festivals to celebrate diversity and inculcate respect for each other among employees and students.

4. Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment
Southeast University places serious emphasis on women's empowerment and gender equality. The university has developed policies for ensuring equal opportunity for female students and staff members to participate in academic, professional, and leadership roles. SEU's gender equality is also evidenced by its efforts to create a harassment-free and safe campus life. The university has also established a special committee to deal with gender-based discrimination and harassment cases, maintaining confidentiality and sensitivity while addressing all complaints.

5. Community Engagement and Social Responsibility
SEU's DEI policy extends beyond the campus, demonstrating its social responsibility and community engagement. The university interacts with the surrounding society and outreach activities, SEU raises awareness of DEI and demands social justice and human rights. These efforts not only benefit the community but also provide a platform for the students to gain hands-on social work experience and develop a sense of civic responsibility.

6. Education and Awareness
(SEU) is committed to fostering an informed and inclusive community through comprehensive education and awareness initiatives. SEU will integrate diversity and inclusion topics into academic curricula, offering courses on global cultures, gender studies, and social justice, drawing inspiration from global liberal arts models to enrich learning. DEI orientation programs will be conducted for new students, faculty, and staff to build awareness and reinforce commitment to these values from the outset. Additionally, SEU will host regular workshops, seminars, and guest lectures on DEI issues, inviting experts and community leaders to share insights, ensuring ongoing dialogue and education to promote a culture of respect and inclusion across the university.

7. Grievance and Redressal
Southeast University (SEU) ensures a robust mechanism to address DEI-related concerns, fostering a safe and equitable environment. Complaints of discrimination, harassment, or exclusion are processed through the SEU Grievance Redress Policy, supported by a dedicated DEI officer who provides guidance and assistance to complainants throughout the resolution process. Whistleblower protections are firmly in place to safeguard individuals reporting DEI violations, guaranteeing confidentiality and shielding them from retaliation encourage fearless reporting. Disciplinary actions for breaches of the DEI policy are enforced in accordance with the SEU Service Rules and may range from warnings to suspensions or termination, depending on the severity of the violation, ensuring accountability and justice within the university community.

8. Challenges and Future Directions
While Southeast University has made significant strides in promoting diversity, equality, and inclusion, there remain challenges to be addressed. Like most institutions in Bangladesh, SEU will be faced with societal and cultural barriers that can impede the full realization of its DEI goals. For instance, entrenched gender stereotypes and socioeconomic disparities can be obstacles to the achievement of real equality. In order to counter these challenges, SEU must continue to innovate and revise its policies so that they remain adaptive and effective in a changing social environment. Going forward, SEU can increase the implementation of more data-oriented methods for tracking the impact of its policies and assessing areas to be improved upon. In addition, the university can further promote engagement with institutions from all over the globe in an effort to understand best practices and enhance its DEI efforts.

Compliance
This policy complies with:
- Private Universities Act, 2010, ensuring equitable education access.
- Bangladesh Constitution, upholding non-discrimination principles.
- Guideline on Prevention and Protection from Sexual Harassment Offence, 2008.
- Digital Security Act, 2018, and other relevant laws protecting rights and safety.

Conclusion
Southeast University's DEI Policy reflects a commitment to building a vibrant, equitable, and inclusive community that drives academic excellence and societal impact. By embracing diversity, ensuring equality, and fostering inclusion, SEU aims to empower every individual to reach their full potential, contributing to a brighter, more inclusive future for Bangladesh and beyond.

clean_text:
Dept. of Business Administration

Welcome to our School of Business Studies where the future leaders of the business world are nurtured and shaped.

Vision & Mission

VISION: To obtain global recognition as a world-class Business School by encouraging and facilitating business education, research, and other scholarly activities to students, faculty members, and other stakeholders.

MISSION: To provide quality higher education in business-oriented discipline to local and international students and raise ethical business professionals who can face the business challenges of the twenty-first century.

PEO and PLO: To instil the moral and ethical values of business among the students, foster human and intellectual capital development and develop leadership skills to transform them into business professionals.

Message from Dean, School of Business Studies (SBS): Pioneering Excellence in Business Education for Future Leaders

Our School of Business Studies embarked on its cherished journey in 2002 with BBA Program along with Computer Science and Engineering. Through its 22 years of journey, it has now become a matured one, and rendering quality education in BBA and MBA Programs. Our main focus is to cater the needs of the society and corporate world. We are highly proactive to create self-employed entrepreneurs, young business executives, academicians, researchers and active manpower of the society. While providing most modern business concepts, ideas, theories of western business education, we are highly committed to make a good blend with social values, norms and cultures of Bangladesh society. To keep pace with the modern world, we are now following Outcome-Based-Education (OBE) curriculum with all requirements and inherent characteristics. Our classrooms are well equipped with all modern teaching aids and connectivity with the world. Our faculty members are also well trained in offering modern OBE curriculum to our participating students. In order to have a good blending of theories and practices, we have a good number of adjunct faculties from corporate world. Our students are not only getting practical knowledge about business world; but also getting exposures to job market requirements. This is helping students tremendously to get them prepared for the job market. On a regular basis, we are also arranging seminars, symposiums, round table conference on most relevant current issues. Through this process, our students are getting more conscious about current social problems and develop themselves as to how manpower challenges of today's society of Bangladesh. Our Business School is also future oriented. In our school, we are trying to develop global operating skills of students to meet the future demand of job market. Through our relentless endeavor, we are gradually trying to become leading Business School of the country. As Dean of the School of Business Studies, I welcome you to join us and build excellent career in near future.

Message from [Head of BBA Program]:

The BBA program at Southeast University is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in business principles while equipping them with the critical thinking, ethical awareness and practical skills necessary for success in today's competitive global market. At SEU, we emphasize both academic excellence and personal development. Our experienced faculty, with expertise from leading universities worldwide, prepares students for real-world difficulties in management, marketing, finance, accounting, and entrepreneurship. We also offer a wide range of extracurricular activities, leadership opportunities, and internships to enhance your learning experience. Whether you are a prospective student, a parent, or an industry partner, I encourage you to explore all that our BBA program has to offer. We are committed to fostering a learning environment that nurtures innovation, leadership, and success.

title: Message from Director
clean_text:
A nation's development potential hinges on the growth of its intellectual capital—defined by the knowledge, skills, and innovative capacity of its people. Education, particularly higher education, plays a pivotal role in cultivating and enhancing these capabilities. Recognizing that Bangladesh's higher education system was not fully equipped to produce graduates with the skills needed for a competitive global economy, the Government of Bangladesh (GoB) identified an urgent need for reform. Without significant improvements, the country risked falling behind in an increasingly knowledge-driven world. To remain competitive, higher education institutions (HEIs) must expand their scope, foster creativity and individuality in students, and develop high-quality human resources capable of driving national progress.

In response, the University Grants Commission (UGC)—serving as the bridge between the government and universities—formulated the "Strategic Plan for Higher Education 2006-2026", outlining a roadmap for the future of higher education in Bangladesh. This plan led to the launch of the Higher Education Quality Enhancement Project (HEQEP) in mid-2009, supported by the World Bank and implemented by the Ministry of Education. Under HEQEP, the Quality Assurance Unit (QAU) was established within the UGC to introduce and oversee quality assurance mechanisms in Bangladeshi HEIs. The QAU has since facilitated the creation of Institutional Quality Assurance Cells (IQACs) in universities, providing guidelines and processes to ensure their effective operation. These efforts aim to elevate teaching, learning, and research standards while embedding a sustainable internal quality assurance system across all HEIs.

In alignment with this national initiative, Southeast University (SEU) has established its own Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) to uphold and advance these critical objectives.

Message from Director

As part of its ongoing commitment to quality assurance, the University Grants Commission (UGC) recommended the establishment of an institutionalized internal quality assurance system at Southeast University (SEU) through the Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) at the university level. Recognizing the importance of providing a high-quality learning experience for students, Southeast University promptly acted on the UGC's directive and established the IQAC. The IQAC is tasked with collaborating closely with academic and administrative units across the university to uphold both internal and external quality assurance standards. In fulfilling its responsibilities, the IQAC will support Southeast University's academic and administrative units in program planning, development, and review. Additionally, it will disseminate quality assurance guidelines and information through various means, including training and advisory services for faculty and administrative staff on key processes.

I am very pleased to state that since January 2019, IQAC has become a permanent educational wing of Southeast University. Working as an independent center, it is dedicated to the greater improvement of the university. I look forward to your valuable support and cooperation in this new journey of IQAC. With your support and kind cooperation, IQAC at SEU can become a pioneer in Higher University Education in Bangladesh.

Prof. Dr. Abdul Kadar Muhammad Masum
Director, IQAC

title: Program Offerings:
clean_text:
Center for Modern Languages (CML) at Southeast University (SEU) is dedicated to fostering cultural exchange, global communication, and language learning. Mastering a language opens doors to international careers and enriches cultural experiences. We invite you to use our comprehensive language programs to enhance your academic and professional growth.

Meet Our Director: Dr. Mohammad Abu Nayeem, Assistant Professor in the Department of English, leads CML with a commitment providing high-quality language instruction and fostering cultural engagement. As a university teacher for 17 years, he has always been enthusiastic about teaching and research. He has published over 15 national and international articles. In addition to instructing Bangladeshi students, he also taught students from other nations and cultures, such as Afghanistan, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Syria, Timore Leste, Vietnam, Yemen, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt. Before joining SEU, he worked as an ESL teacher at the Asian University for Women, Southeast University, the University of Asia Pacific, BGMEA University, and SMP in Saudi Arabia. He pursued an MA in TESOL from North South University in 2007 and obtained PhD from Jadavpur University, India.

CML at SEU is a dynamic language center that provides linguistic skills and cultural awareness to individuals of all ages and backgrounds. Whether you're a student, professional, homemaker, or immigrant, we offer comprehensive language programs designed to help you thrive in today's interconnected world.

Program Offerings:
ESL Courses: Our ESL curriculum is designed to be practical and comprehensive, catering to learners of all proficiency levels, from beginner to advanced. We offer intensive courses on speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills and specialized classes for business communication, academic English, Spoken English, Phonetics, Professional English, and TOEFL/IELTS preparation. We also offer courses tailored explicitly for homemakers and parents, ensuring everyone can find a course that suits their needs.

Foreign Language Courses: The Center for Modern Languages will offer a wide range of language courses, reflecting the linguistic diversity of our community. Whether and knowledge, will guide them through the journey of language acquisition.

Test Preparation: CML will serve as a testing center for language proficiency exams, including standardized tests such as the TOEFL, IELTS, and Cambridge English exams. Our certified examiners will ensure the integrity and validity of the testing process, providing reliable assessment results for individuals and institutions.

Cultural Events and Workshops: CML will host various cultural events, workshops, and seminars to foster cross-cultural understanding and appreciation. These activities will allow students to engage with native speakers, explore different customs and traditions, and broaden their global perspectives.

Facilities and Resources: CML will have modern classrooms, multimedia laboratories, a library/resource center, and comfortable study areas. We will utilize cutting-edge technology and digital resources to enhance the learning experience and provide students access to online materials and language-learning software.

Why Learn with Us?
Cultural Exposure: Gain insights into diverse cultures through immersive language learning.
Career Advancement: Enhance your career prospects with multilingual skills in a global job market.
International Collaboration: Participate in seminars and events that connect you with global scholars, professionals, and industry leaders.

Partnerships & Collaborations:
Collaborating with Global Institutions: Soon we will collaborate with organizations like the British Council and the American Center to offer exciting student opportunities, including exchange programs, joint educational ventures, and access to global resources. For other languages, we have a plan to make partnerships with the following: Confucius Institute, Goethe Institut, Nippon Academy, Alliance française.

title: Journal Information in Short:
clean_text:
Southeast University Journal of Architecture (SEUJA) is a bi-annual, peer-reviewed journal publishing research on architecture, urbanism, design, and building technologies. It is open access with no submission or processing fees. Papers can be submitted anytime via email and are reviewed for quality and relevance. Published articles are freely accessible through academic databases and repositories.

The "Southeast University Journal of Architecture" offers architects, academics and researchers opportunities for accessing and sharing knowledge on various aspects of the built environment and be a part of a more speculative design environment. Articles and writings would include critical thinking on architecture, town planning and urbanism, landscape design, interior design, building technology, construction methods and structure systems, management of historic buildings and urban landscapes and art in architecture. This journal publishes articles bi-annually with a single-blind peer-reviewed policy. The journal is published both in printed format and online edition. There is no article submission and processing fee (No APCs). Two issues are published in a year (June and December). The author(s) can submit the paper(s) anytime, through email. Journal sends an acknowledgement of paper submission first and puts it in the primary editorial process for checking the plagiarism, contribution and relevance to the scope of the journal. SEUJA provides the research article(s) to the target audience through academic search engines, repositories, and social media. The scientific community uses published papers of the journal without any paywall (No APCs) copyright restrictions for quality research.

title: Campus Life
clean_text:
Southeast University features a modern, well-furnished cafeteria with a seating capacity of 200, designed to create a comfortable and welcoming environment. It offers a variety of high-quality food and beverages at competitive prices, catering to the diverse tastes of students and staff. The cafeteria ensures excellent service, hygiene, and a diverse menu to meet everyone's needs. Beyond being a place to enjoy meals, it functions as a lively social hub, encouraging interaction, collaboration, and fostering a sense of belonging among students, faculty, and staff throughout the day.

The SEU Library serves as a vital resource for students and faculty, offering a spacious, modern, and well-equipped environment for study and research. With an extensive collection of texts, reference books, journals, and newspapers, the library aims to provide high-quality educational materials. It is accessible to all faculty, staff, and students, featuring air-conditioned, open-shelved spaces for comfortable browsing and study. The library is fully computerized and connected to the internet, allowing users to access a wealth of academic resources remotely through Integrated Library Management System software "KOHA". Additionally, the library is a part of an international consortium, enabling the downloading of valuable articles, and has subscriptions to prominent e-resources like IEEEXplore, Emerald Insight and the Manupatra legal database. With amenities such as free Wi-Fi, computers, and printers, the SEU Library encourages students to take full advantage of these resources for their academic pursuits.

Southeast University's Indoor Game Zone offers students a dynamic recreational space to relax and participate in different activities. Equipped with facilities for billiards, table tennis, chess, and carrom, it provides a perfect environment for friendly competition and relaxation. The zone fosters social interaction and teamwork, helping students maintain a healthy balance between academics and leisure. SEU game zone gives a comfortable environment that encourages mental well-being and helps to bring the university community together.

Southeast University (SEU) operates a well-equipped medical center on the ground floor of the campus, offering essential healthcare services to students, faculty, and staff. The center is staffed by experienced MBBS doctors, with one of them being a BCS cadre physician, ensuring high-quality medical care. It provides medical consultation and refers patients to specialized doctors when necessary. The center administers first aid, manages emergencies, and arranges transportation to the nearest hospital through SEU transport if required. In emergencies, essential medicines are supplied, and proper nursing care is provided when needed. Additionally, the medical team verifies student medical documents for semester drops and refunds, ensuring seamless administrative support. The SEU Medical Center plays a vital role in promoting the health and well-being of the university community. The center is open daily.

The SEU Multipurpose Hall is a state-of-the-art facility with a seating capacity of 600, thoughtfully designed to accommodate a wide range events throughout the year. It features a spacious stage equipped with advanced audio-visual technology, ensuring smooth and professional performances, presentations, and ceremonies. The hall's versatility makes it ideal for hosting academic conferences, cultural programs, corporate events, and community gatherings. With comfortable seating, excellent acoustics, and modern amenities, the multipurpose hall serves as a dynamic venue that enhances the experience of every event, leaving a lasting impression on attendees.

Given its motto, "Meeting the challenges of Time" the university is always introducing new programs and soft-skill development initiatives. The university aims to provide up-to-date education, hands-on application, and research facilities to its students. SEU has always strived to provide higher education at an affordable cost, considering the economic conditions of the middle and lowermiddle-income families in Bangladesh. SEU aims to impart worldclass education and help students reach their highest capacities. On the occasion of the holy month of Ramadan, Southeast University organized a discussion meeting on the significance of Ramadan followed by an Iftar Mahfil. The program was held at the university's Multipurpose Hall. Mr. Rezaul Karim, Honorable Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Southeast University, attended the program as the Chief Guest. Advocate Niaz Ahmed, Honorable Member of the Board of Trustees, was present as the Special Discussant. The event was presided over by Professor Dr. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, Vice Chancellor of Southeast University. innovators, and professionals dedicated to advancing knowledge and addressing the challenges of the future. Our School is home to five dynamic departments:

1. Department of Computer Science & Engineering: Leading the way in cutting-edge research, technology, and software development, our programs prepare students to be pioneers in the rapidly evolving world of computing and information technology.

2. Department of Architecture: Combining creativity with technical expertise, our Architecture programs foster the development of innovative designs that are both functional and sustainable, shaping the built environment of tomorrow.

3. Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering: From microelectronics to power systems, our programs equip students with the skills to develop advanced technologies and solutions for the modern world, driving innovation across various industries.

We are excited to have you join our community and look forward to supporting your academic journey and professional growth. Together, let us work towards creating a brighter, more innovative future.

title: Professor Mohammed Shamsul Hoque, Ph.D.
clean_text:
Welcome to the School of Arts and Social Sciences (SASS) at Southeast University, where education in general is provided to help curiosity meet purpose and achievement ensure empathy. Here, students and faculty probe society, interpret culture, and examine the human condition, engaging thoughtfully with emerging technologies like AI connect learning with societal and industry ecosystems. Our programs are designed to be both relevant and transformative, fostering insights into human behavior and the complexities of our shared world. In an era of rapid technological change and global connectivity, the arts and social sciences are vital for understanding, questioning, and shaping society and the world at large. At SASS, we nurture graduates to seek knowledge with a purpose, reflect on what they learn and how they will use their knowledge for the greater good of the whole human race. We empower our learning community to be personally responsible, socially concerned, morally sound, and professionally proactive. Through interdisciplinary learning, research, and community engagement, students explore ideas beyond disciplinary boundaries and connect scholarships to real-world challenges. Our faculty guide learners to study contemporary issues through critical analysis, ethical reflection, and informed discourse. The achievements of our alumni across academia, public service, media, development, and creative industries reflect the enduring impact of a SASS education at SEU.

As the Dean of the School of Arts & Social Sciences (SASS), I am heartily welcoming you to the SASS, as we believe that by dint of our dynamic and effective leadership, our school would be the perfect choice for developing your career. I ardently invite students, scholars, parents, and partners to join us in this journey of discovery, self-empowerment and community commitment.

Professor Mohammed Shamsul Hoque, Ph.D.
Dean, School of Arts and Social Sciences
Southeast University

title: PEO Description
clean_text:
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) After 3 to 5 years of completion of Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering program, the graduates would be able (to show the following qualities):

PEO Description
---
PEO1 To engage themselves in lifelong pursuit of knowledge and interdisciplinary education, science, research and project management, academic career, leadership, and entrepreneurial development.
PEO2 To contribute to the welfare and sustainable development of the society through the use of computer science and engineering principles, practices, and tools in ethical and responsible ways.
PEO3 To establish themselves as leading computational professionals and/or entrepreneurs; and continue to learn and address evolving challenges in computer science and engineering.
PEO4 To excel as a professional in computing by enhancing the knowledge, problem-solving, problem analyzing, designing, investigating, teamwork, and communication skills.

Program Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of Bachelor of Science Computer Science and Engineering program the students will be able to obtain the following knowledge and skills:

PLO Description
---
PLO1 Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization respectively to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PLO2 Identify, formulate, research issues and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences and engineering sciences.
PLO3 Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design systems, components or processes that meet specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
PLO4 Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions.
PLO5 Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering problems, with an understanding of the limitations.
PLO6 Apply reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional engineering practice and solutions to complex engineering problems.
PLO7 Understand and evaluate the sustainability and impact of professional engineering work in the solution of complex engineering problems in societal and environmental contexts.
PLO8 Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of engineering practice.

title: Seminar On Competitive Programming A Pathway To Success Through Skill Development
clean_text: The Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Southeast University organized a seminar on Competitive Programming: Pathway to Success Through Skill Development at the university permanent campus situated at Tejgaon. The interactive session commenced with an opening speech by Tashreef Muhammad, Lecturer and one of the coordinators of the department who acted as the host. He welcomed everyone and thanked the guest speakers for their cooperation to help organize the event. He shared some of his student life experiences and his ideology that programming is more about keeping on trying with dedication until the further end. Mr. Nazrul Islam, Lecturer of the department shared invaluable insight with the students and motivated them to practice coding as a competitive game. He explained that self-improvement is observed by others, not by oneself. Hence, one should keep on trying and never give up as oneself might not understand but everyone around will see the improvement as days go by. Md. Shamim, who is also a lecturer of the department shared his thoughts and ideas on how Competitive Programming helps improve thinking capacity and implores one to gain a great advantage over everything. He explained that by training the brain from as early stage as possible, the brain develops to become more efficient. He also shared how he thought mastering programming seemed like magic to him during his younger days. Finally, the department Chair and Associate Professor, Shahriar Manzoor, shared his invaluable thoughts with the students from his beginner days till his recent interactions including the time he spent as the final round judge ACM ICPC and explored with the students about different career options relating and circled around competitive programming. He brought up success stories of many of the past contestants during his session including the ones graduated from Southeast University. The program ended with an interactive Question Answering session. The host concluded the session with a vote of thanks. The event will help develop student's interest in delving deeper into competitive programming.

Biography:
Prof. Dr Yusuf Mahbubul Islam is currently the Vice Chancellor of Southeast University, Dhaka, Bangladesh, where he has been serving since May 2024. His academic leadership and innovative approaches in higher education have been influential in the development of digital learning platforms and the integration of technology into education management. Prof Dr Yusuf Mahbubul Islam has more than 46 years of teaching, research, and administrative experience different institutions in Bangladesh, the United Kingdom, and Malaysia. Before joining Southeast University, Prof. Yusuf held numerous prominent roles in higher education institutions. From January 2023 to February 2024, he was the Director of Graduate Studies, Research, and Industry Relations at Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), and from October 2022 to February 2024, he also served as a Professor at IUB. He led as Dean of the School of Engineering Technology and Sciences (SETS) from September 2020 to October 2022, contributing significantly to research and academic growth. Prof. Yusuf also chairs the Institute for the Development of Online Learning (IDOL), a position he has held since June 2020, where he leads efforts to promote competency-based online learning for both individuals and institutions. His expertise in online education and training methodologies has made him a pivotal figure in this domain. At Daffodil International University (DIU), Yusuf had a long and impactful tenure, spanning from 2010 to February 2024, during which he served as a Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and Executive Director of the Human Resources Development Institute (HRDI). His tenure as Vice Chancellor of DIU from July 2015 to April 2020 marked a period of remarkable growth, with student numbers doubling and research output expanding significantly. Prof. Yusuf's career also includes a strong background in software development, having served as Managing Director of Soft-Ed Ltd from September 1995 to December 2002, where he developed key software systems for industries across Bangladesh.

title: Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
clean_text:
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
The Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Electronic Engineering (BSc in EEE) program of Southeast University (SEU) and its curriculum are designed to provide the fundamental knowledge and principles of engineering and science, and the broad general education knowledge for the continued professional growth of its graduates. The general objectives of the 4-year BSc in EEE program are to prepare the graduates to become successful in their chosen career paths. The program educational objectives (PEOs) of the BSc in EEE program have been set in such a way that after 3-5 years of graduation the graduates can demonstrate their ability to:

PEO Descriptions
---
---
PEO1: Expertise: Demonstrate their capability as electrical and electronic engineers by acquiring the complex engineering problem-solving skills and knowledge, team-work abilities, and communication skills during their study in the program.
PEO2: Enhancement: Enhance professional growth continuously through post-graduate education, continuing education or professional activities or training or licensure, and thus participate in lifelong-learning activities that develop their confidence level and sustainability in the job market.
PEO3: Engagement: Engage technical or business activities professionally and ethically through electrical and electronic engineering knowledge, social justice, leadership roles and responsibilities, communication and other soft skills and thus make professional contributions to the society.
PEO4: Contribution: Contribute to the national level in the areas of electrical and electronic engineering and thus contribute the progress and development of the country.

Program Outcomes
The program outcomes (POs) of the EEE department of Southeast University (SEU) have been set in such a way so that after graduation the students can demonstrate the ability to-

PO Descriptions
---
---
[PO1] Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex electrical and electronic engineering problems;
[PO2] Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, research the literature and analyze complex electrical and electronic engineering problems and reach substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, the natural sciences and the engineering sciences.
[PO3] Design/ Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex electrical and electronic engineering problems and design systems, components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for manufacturability and sustainability, public health and safety as well as cultural, societal, economic, political, ethical and environmental concerns;
[PO4] Investigation: Conduct investigations of complex electrical and electronic engineering problems, considering design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions;
[PO5] Modern Tool Usage: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex electrical and electronic engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations;
[PO6] The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning informed by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional electrical and electronic engineering practice;
[PO7] Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of professional electrical and electronic engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development;
[PO8] Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, responsibilities and the norms of the electrical and electronic engineering practice;
[PO9] Individual Work and Teamwork: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader of diverse teams as well as in multidisciplinary settings;
[PO10] Communication: Communicate effectively about complex electrical and electronic engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large. Be able to comprehend and write effective reports, design documentation, make effective presentations and give and receive clear instructions;
[PO11] Project Management and Finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the electrical and electronic engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work as a member or a leader of a team to manage projects in multidisciplinary environments;
[PO12] Life-long learning: Recognize the need for and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent, life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

title: Seminar On Connecting Minds Microchips Eee Dept
clean_text: The Department of EEE and IEEE SEU Student Branch jointly organized a seminar titled "Connecting Minds & Microchips" featuring Sirajul Alam Khan, Founder & CEO of SILICONOVA, as the keynote speaker. As one of the leading companies in VLSI and microchip design, SILICONOVA is equipped with state-of-the-art tools like Cadence and advanced verification platforms. Mr. Khan inspired students to explore exciting career opportunities in microchip design and welcomed SEU students to receive training from SILICONOVA. title: Industry Visit To Cybernetics Hi Tech Solutions Eee
clean_text: The Department of EEE recently organized an enriching industrial visit to Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions, a pioneering private tech firm in Bangladesh known for its cutting-edge work in robotics, automation, and embedded systems. The company, a sister concern of Spectrum Engineering Consortium Ltd., has made headlines with innovations like "Jontro Soinik 1.0"—Bangladesh's first indigenously developed EOD robot for defense applications. Led by faculty members Dr. Md. Asif Hossain, Mr. Tawsif Hossain Chowdhury, Mr. Md. Rounakul Islam, and Mr. Md. Saifur Rahman, a group of 27 enthusiastic EEE students explored the facility, witnessed real-time R&D in action, and engaged in an inspiring session with CEO & MD Rashed Mujib Noman. The visit provided EEE students with hands-on exposure to robotics and embedded systems, along with insights into careers in industrial and defense technology. It also opened doors for future academic-industry collaboration, bridging the gap between classroom learning and real-world innovation.

title: Texcellence 20 A Grand Celebration Of Textile Innovation And Culture At Seu
clean_text: Texcellence 2.0 – A Grand Celebration of Textile Innovation and Culture at Southeast University The Department of Textile Engineering, Southeast University, in collaboration with the Southeast Textile Club, successfully hosted Texcellence 2.0 at the university's permanent campus in Tejgaon, Dhaka. The event brought together university leaders, distinguished alumni, industry pioneers, and young textile talents under one platform to celebrate innovation, creativity, and knowledge-sharing in the textile and apparel sector. The program was inaugurated by Prof. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, PhD, the Vice Chancellor. The event was graced by respected university guests, including Prof. Dr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro Vice Chancellor; Major General Anwarul Islam, SUP, ndu, psc (Retd), the Registrar; Prof. Engr. Masud Ahmed, Chairman of the Department Textile Engineering; and Dr. Md. Shamim Alam, an Associate Professor and Moderator of the Southeast Textile Club. Syed Iftakhar Ahmad, Assistant Moderator of the Southeast Textile Club. The event was led by Md Manik Miah, President of the Southeast Textile Club, and, along with dedicated faculty members and students. Notable Alumni including Mohammad Hasnat Hossain, Head of Advisory Committee, SEUTEX, Foysal Ahmed, and Rashduzzaman Siddique Jitu inspired students by sharing their professional journeys and insights. The event also witnessed the participation of renowned industry leaders, such as Md. Atiqur Rahman Manik (Acme Garments Unit), Kamal Uddin Mia (Bitopi Group), Md. Reza E Rabbi (Vertex Wear Ltd.), Kiron Morshed (Vertex RMG Division), Rehan Asif (Pepco Global Sourcing), Md. Imrul Quaesh (NEXT Sourcing Bangladesh), Farhana Rahman Mitu (Marks and Spencer), Krishan Bhowmik (IDKids Okaidi France), Md. Faisal Rashid Khan & Azmal Hossain (Anko Sourcing – Target Australia BD Liaison Office), Engr. Raju Ahmed Rajon (Sterling Group), Md. Tazul Islam (Islam Group Ltd.), and S.M. Prosun-uz-zaman Khan Rezu (RNT BD Ltd., Riztu Corporation) among others. Their participation created valuable networking opportunities, industry-academia linkages, and pathways for job placements and internships for students. Md. Rubaiet Ibn Raihan, Facilitator & Engagement Strategist of the event and a professional from Anko Sourcing (Target Australia BD Liaison Office), ensured seamless coordination between students, faculty, and industry guests, making Texcellence 2.0 an engaging and impactful experience. The program featured a diverse lineup of events under the theme "Tex Talk", including seminars, panel discussions, wall magazine competitions, the Brain Buzz quiz, and TexStyle fashion ramp shows highlighting Bangladeshi culture. Several universities including BUTEX, BUFT, AUST, NUB, IUBAT, MBSTU and Uttara University participated, making it a collaborative platform for future textile leaders. The success of Texcellence 2.0 was further amplified by the generous support of sponsors RNT (BD) Ltd., Riztu Corporation, Officina 39, and Gold Royals – Sustainable Solution. Speaking on the occasion, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, PhD, praised the initiative for bridging academia with industry, while industry leaders commended the students' creativity and professionalism. With vibrant participation, academic-industry collaboration, and the creation of multiple job opportunities, Texcellence 2.0 stands as a milestone event in Southeast University's journey of nurturing the next generation of textile professionals.

title: Prof. Engr. Mashud Ahmed
clean_text:
Prof. Engr. Mashud Ahmed
Chairman & Professor
Room: 304, 3rd Floor
tex.chair@seu.edu.bd, mashud.ahmed@seu.edu.bd

Biography
Prof. Mashud Ahmed is a distinguished figure in textile technology, celebrated for his academic and professional contributions. He began his educational journey at the University of Dhaka, graduating in 1980 as part of the first batch of the B.Sc. in Textile Technology program. In 1985, he was awarded the Canadian Commonwealth Scholarship, allowing him to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Guelph in Canada, where he completed his M.Sc. in Consumer Studies (Textile Science) in 1986. He then enrolled in the PhD program in the Department of Chemistry at the same university, continuing his studies until 1988, but was unable to complete his doctoral degree due to inadequate facilities.

Prof. Ahmed's extensive experience includes significant leadership roles in academia and industry. He served as the Vice-Chancellor of the Bangladesh University of Textiles and was the Dean of the Faculty of Textile Manufacturing Engineering at the same institution since its inception. Additionally, he has been a member of the Syndicate and Academic Council of the Bangladesh University of Textiles since the university was established. His practical experience includes working with the Bangladesh Textile Mill Corporation, which has enriched his understanding of the textile industry.

Currently, he holds the position of Professor and Chairman at the Department of Textile Engineering at Southeast University (SEU) since 2023, where he also serves as the Acting Dean. Prof. Ahmed has been actively involved in various professional organizations, including the Textile Institute in Manchester, UK, and the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh, where he is a Fellow Life Member. He is also a Life Member of the Institution of Textile Engineers & Technologists in Bangladesh and a Senior Member of the American Association of Textile Chemists & Colorists. His extensive professional affiliations reflect his commitment to advancing textile science both academically and practically.

Prof. Ahmed's legacy continues to inspire students and professionals alike, as he advocates for innovation and excellence within the textile industry.

Biography
Prof. Dr. Arun Kanti Guha has been serving as Treasurer of Southeast University. Bangladesh since February, 2023. Prof. Guha was born in 1970. He received BSc (Honours) and MSc in Chemistry from University of Dhaka in 1990 and 1991 respectively. He received PhD in 2000 from the Department of Chemistry, Inha University, South Korea. Prof. Guha also completed postdoctoral research from the same University of South Korea. Prof. Guha is a recipient of Korean Govt. Scholarship (BK21) and postdoctoral fellowship of Korea Research Foundation (KRF) respectively. He has a combination of teaching, research and work experiences in the field of chemistry and textile environmental pollution control for the last 28 years. Before joining Southeast University, he worked as a faculty member in Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB). Prof. Guha published scientific papers in peer reviewed international indexed journals published by Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC), American Chemical Society (ACS) and Wiley. Prof. Guha is reviewer of national and international peer reviewed journals. Prof. Guha is also an external examiner of overseas PhD Thesis. Research interests of Prof. Guha are organic synthesis, reaction mechanism study, pollution control, effluent treatment and sludge management.

title: BSc Architecture Curriculum
clean_text:
BSc Architecture Curriculum

The Department of Architecture at Southeast University offers a Bachelor of Science in Architecture program. The curriculum is designed to provide students with comprehensive knowledge and skills in architectural design, theory, and practice. The program focuses on developing students' abilities to create functional, aesthetically pleasing, and sustainable architectural solutions.

The department is committed to guiding students in education through a balanced approach that combines theoretical knowledge with practical application. Students are trained to develop critical thinking, design reasoning, and professional skills needed in the architectural field.

The program emphasizes experimentation and the integration of evolving technologies in architectural design and practice. Students learn to grasp the meaning and context of architectural spaces while developing their unique design perspectives.

PEO1: Possess basic and advanced knowledge relevant to architecture, providing innovative ideas for conventional solutions in the field of architecture profession and pursue higher studies and career in research.

PO3: Develop concepts, design, solutions and artworks responding to the problem through the application of theoretical knowledge, physical survey, inter- relationship between people, buildings and the environment.
PO4: Articulate an appropriate philosophical approach to problems through investigations which reveals an understanding of theory in a cultural context and critically evaluate methodologies, architectural theories, graphics presentations and propose new and original hypotheses.
