Tucked in a quiet grove, "The Secret Phonebooth" suspends between trees—two translucent volumes linked by a green mesh triangle. Made from simple materials like cellophane and spiral pipe, it evokes memories of childhood tin-can phones, private conversations, and quiet nostalgia in nature. More than a structure, it captures a fleeting, intimate moment in time.

title: Dr. Masud Ur Rashid
clean_text:
Dr. Masud Ur Rashid
Chairman & Professor
Room: 522, 5th Floor
arch.chair@seu.edu.bd, masud.rashid@seu.edu.bd
Biography
Dr. Masud Ur Rashid (B.Arch, M.Arch, PhD) is a renowned Bangladeshi architect and researcher widely recognised for his significant contributions to urban and rural sociology, housing, human settlement, and sustainability in the built environment. He currently serves as the Professor and Chairman at the Department Architecture, Southeast University. His research primarily focuses on socio-economic and environmental issues affecting human settlements, with a particular interest in: Housing and Settlement: Exploring affordable housing solutions, transformation of housing in low-income settlements, and the role of home-based enterprises in housing transformation. Sustainability and Resilience: Investigating the sustainability and resilience of living environments, including climate change adaptation in built forms and energy-driven design development. Urban and Rural Sociology: Studying generic settlement patterns, especially in the Bengal Delta, and the impact of cultural heritages on rural housing. He has authored numerous articles and publications in reputed local and international journals, contributing significantly to the academic discourse in these areas. His publications include works on the Bengal Delta's definition and anthropogenic aspects, negotiation with domestic units by middle-class households, and studies on vernacular wisdom in Asian architecture. He has also penned working papers, such as "Hundred Homes for Rural Poor" for the Institute of Architects Bangladesh (IAB). He serves as a member of the editorial board and reviewer in different reputed journals, both in the local and international arena. Beyond his academic and research endeavours, Dr. Masud Ur Rashid is actively involved in professional organisations. He currently serves as the General Secretary of the Institute of Architects Bangladesh (IAB). His leadership extends to various roles in architectural competitions and workshops, including serving as a competition director for open architectural design competitions. He is a member of the UIA (International Union of Architects) Work Programme on Social Habitat. He is representing Bangladesh in the ARCASIA Committee on Young Architects (ACYA) and the ARCASIA Committee on Social Responsibilities (ACSR). His expertise is recognised through various accolades, including being consistently ranked among the top researchers in Architecture in Bangladesh by the AD Scientific Index. Dr. Masud Ur Rashid's work exemplifies a commitment to understanding and addressing the complex challenges of human habitat, blending academic rigour with practical applications in the architectural field.

The Bachelor of Social Sciences (BSS Hons) in Economics serves the students with practical and updated knowledge of Economics. PEO Descriptions --- --- PEO1: Specialized Knowledge: Possess specialized knowledge about the theories and models related to the different branches core and applied economics, international trade, project planning, research methodology, statistics, sociology, and development economics. PEO2: Professionalism: Exhibit professionalism in both managerial and entrepreneurial fields and high quality of critical thinking, problem solving, decision making, adaptive and time management and leadership capacities, communication skills and innovativeness. PEO3: Quality: Demonstrate high quality of knowledge and technical skills to conduct both qualitative and quantitative research independently on the socioeconomic issues at both national and international levels. PEO4: Awareness: Display a high level of awareness about the various aspects of social and economic problems, climate change and its impacts on society and work towards the improvement of the society. PEO5: Principles: Exhibit high quality of ethical, moral, legal and professional principles and responsibilities in both individual and team works. PEO6: Lifelong learning: Reveal an aptitude for lifelong learning to cope up with the advancements in different fields of economics and continuous professional development for meeting the challenges to discharge professional responsibilities and contribute to equitable and sustainable development. Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs) Upon successful completion of the B.S.S. (Hons) in Economics program, students will be able to: PLO Descriptions --- --- PLO1: Demonstrate Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge about the different theories and models related to the different branches of core and applied economics, international trade, project planning, research methodology, statistics, and development economics. PLO2: Apply Theoretical and Analytical Skills: Apply their theoretical knowledge and analytical skills using statistical and mathematical tools to critically evaluate economic viability and sustainability of different approaches. PLO3: Demonstrate Professionalism: Demonstrate professionalism in managerial field through guidance, support, planning, team building, negotiating, time management and supervision. PLO4: Communicate: Communicate fluently and spontaneously to peers, experts and non-experts and work closely with people of various levels and present themselves at the local, national, and international forums maintaining legal, moral, ethical and professional codes of conduct. PLO5: Analyze: Analyze the needs of the different segments of the society, social and economic disparities, climate change and its impacts on Bangladesh and employ them for the improvement of society with maximum participation. PLO6: Apply: Apply the theories and policies related to national and international trade and finance and analyze the impacts of those policies aggregate economic activities. PLO7: Evaluate Risks and Uncertainties: Evaluate risks and uncertainties to improve individual ability of problem solving, decision making, practicing professionalism and critical thinking in both favorable and complex situations. PLO8: Conduct Research: Conduct research on social and economic aspects using analytical tools and techniques, and incorporate modern digital applications to assemble and analyze information and data and drawing conclusions regarding research problems. PLO9: Practice knowledge and technical skills: Practice knowledge and technical skills to become innovative, risk lover, creative, and passionate entrepreneur. PLO10: Organize and Lead: Apply the knowledge of economics to organize and lead cohesive teams with people having integrity, honesty, and punctuality to address social and economic issues. PLO11: Formulate policies: Estimate the needs and demands for natural and economic resources and formulate policies to ensure optimal use of resources. PLO12: Lifelong learning: Demonstrate and extend the knowledge of economics for lifelong learning to cope with the advancements in different fields of economics and continuous professional development for meeting the emerging challenges. title: Department of Economics Holds Productive Meeting with IQAC Director on BAC Accreditation
clean_text:
Department of Economics Holds Productive Meeting with IQAC Director on BAC Accreditation

The Program Self-Assessment Committee (PSAC) members of the Department of Economics from both the BSS and MDS programs held a constructive meeting with the Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) Director, Prof. Dr. Abdul Kadar Muhammad Masum. From the BSS program, the PSAC team included Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman, Department of Economics, (Convener); Fahima Kabir, Assistant Professor (Member); and Hasan Mehedi, Lecturer (Member). Representing the MDS program, the team comprised Ms. Ruba Rummana, Associate Professor (Convener); Dr. Wasim Akram, Assistant Professor (Member); and Md. Mominul Islam, Lecturer (Member). The meeting focused on motivating the department towards achieving Bangladesh Accreditation Council (BAC) accreditation and clarifying key issues related to preparation activities. Prof. Dr. Masum provided valuable guidance and shared insights to streamline the process. With the dedication of the PSAC members and the support of IQAC, the Department of Economics is confident that these efforts will not only ensure a smooth accreditation journey but also significantly enhance the quality of education for students.

title: Department Of Economics Seu Hosts Youthonomics Ideas Expectations From You
clean_text: The Department of Economics at Southeast University (SEU), in collaboration with the South Asian Network on Economic Modeling (SANEM) and in association with the Young Economists of SEU, organized a special event titled "Youthonomics – Ideas & Expectations from You". The program was graced by renowned economist Professor Dr. Selim Raihan, Professor of Economics at the University of Dhaka and Executive Director of SANEM, who attended as the Chief Guest. Distinguished guests from SANEM included Zubayer Hossen, Program Director and Coordinator of the Sustainability Center; Afsana Ahmed, Program Associate; and Faiyaz Ibne Kabir and Fahmida Farzana, Communication Associates. The event was also attended by Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman of the Department of Economics, along with other respected faculty members. In his keynote speech, Professor Dr. Selim Raihan emphasized the critical importance of understanding economics in today's world, particularly in addressing inequality and fostering inclusive growth. His thought-provoking remarks offered valuable insights for both students and faculty. Following the keynote, SANEM representatives introduced the Youthonomics initiative, which aims to engage young people in economic discourse. The session included interactive discussions where students actively shared their ideas and expectations, making the program lively and participatory. The event concluded with a vote of thanks from Sazeda Akter, Lecturer, Department of Economics, after which tokens of appreciation were presented to the guests on behalf of Southeast University.

title: Mou Signed Between The Department Of Economics
clean_text: MoU Signed Between the Department of Economics, SEU and SANEM The Department of Economics, Southeast University (SEU) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the South Asian Network on Economic Modeling (SANEM) for a collaboration aimed at advancing research, fostering knowledge sharing, and nurturing the next generation of economists. The signing ceremony was attended by Prof. Dr. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, Vice Chancellor of SEU; Prof. Dr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro-Vice Chancellor; Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman, Department of Economics; Dr. Selim Raihan, Executive Director of SANEM; Mr. Zubayer Hossen, Program Director of SANEM; along with esteemed faculty members of SEU. This partnership creates opportunities for impactful academic and policy-oriented research, joint initiatives, capacity-building programs, and greater industry-academia collaboration. The Department of Economics, Southeast University extends heartfelt gratitude to all who contributed to making this event a success.

title: BA (Hons) in English Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) and PLOs
clean_text:
BA (Hons) in English Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) and PLOs

Program Educational Objectives (PEOs): Upon completing of the BA in English program, students will be able to:

PEO1: Practice fundamental, advanced and practical knowledge in the fields of English Language, Literature, Linguistics and English Language Teaching and advance in academic, professional and research careers

PEO2: Demonstrate essential literary, language and research skills that make them confident to create new knowledge, analyze, identify, formulate and solve issues associated with English Language, Literature, Linguistics and English Language Teaching.

PEO3: Engage in individual work, team work, projects, and prosper in their academic and professional careers through innovation, entrepreneurship, leadership, communication and problem-solving skills, and transform themselves into human capital.

PEO4: Use ICT tools to produce, preserve, and present documents and other materials, communicate and interact effectively for social, academic and professional purposes and exhibit ethics, responsibilities and norms of the 21st century life and workplace, and inculcates moral values and ethical standards in congruence with national and international culture and tradition.

PEO5: Develop an understanding of the importance of lifelong learning to cope with the advancements in different areas of English Language, Literature, Linguistics and English Language Teaching, and identify the impact of the use of language and literature in communicating environmental issues and raise awareness of individual responsibilities to preserve and conserve the environment for sustainable development.

Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs): After successful completion of the program, students will be able to:

PLO1: Demonstrate the knowledge of diverse literary genres including fiction and non-fiction as well as the history, theories, and functions of English language, literature, English Language Teaching (ELT) & Linguistics.

PLO2: Analyze and interpret different texts and issues related to English language, literature, ELT & Linguistics along with the ways philosophical and historical movements, and cultural contexts shape and influence texts and interpretations.

PLO3: Create diverse interpretations by applying different literary, linguistic and ELT theories, and use innovative approaches, methods and techniques in teaching and learning.

PLO4: Apply knowledge and skills to conduct research independently in the fields of Literature, English Language Teaching.

PLO5: Use ICT tools to produce, preserve, and present documents and other materials.

PLO6: Demonstrate expertise in the use of language and literature; distinguish diverse social structures and global cultures to incorporate these in personal, social and professional lives.

PLO7: Identify the impact of the use of language and literature in communicating environmental issues and develop the awareness of individual responsibilities to preserve and conserve the environment for sustainable development.

PLO8: Develop ethical and moral values and practice them in personal and professional lives in congruence with national culture and tradition.

PLO9: Develop capabilities for accomplishing tasks of a team or an organization, and function effectively as an individual, a member, and/or a leader, and compete globally in academic and professional fields.

PLO10: Communicate their thoughts and ideas fluently and accurately in both oral and written forms to the audiences at different levels.

PLO11: Exhibit project management skills (preparing assignments, presentations, term papers, reports, dissertations, etc.), and life skills (interpersonal skills, decision-making and problem-solving skills, critical and creative thinking skills, self-awareness and empathy, assertiveness and self-control).

PLO12: Assess the significance of autonomous and life-long learning, and develop the ability to apply their learning into practice throughout their lives.

title: PEO Descriptions
clean_text:
Southeast Business School Program Educational Objectives (PEOs): Upon completion of the BBA Program from the Business School, the students will be able to-

PEO Descriptions
---
PEO1: Possess fundamental, technical and advanced knowledge in various fields of business ensuring adaptability to the local and global environment.
PEO2: Ensure a collaborative educational environment to engage in personal and professional development including self-motivation, self-awareness, leadership, entrepreneurship, innovation and effective communication skills along with theoretical and practical skills transforming them into professional business executives.
PEO3: Demonstrate essential technical and research skills that make them confident to create new knowledge, analyze, identify, formulate and solve issues related to industry or research institutes both home and abroad under various practical constraints.
PEO4: Engage and flourish professional careers through teamwork, innovation and proactive involvement to contribute functional expertise on interdisciplinary teams creating solutions to complex problems.
PEO5: Develop ethical standards improving integrity, morality, honesty, etc. through academic programs, seminars and symposiums for the betterment of society.
PEO6: Inculcate life-long learning through exploring innovation of business opportunities and strategies to address the needs of an ever-changing business environment.

Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs): After the completion of four-year BBA Program, the students will be able to-

PLO Descriptions
---
PLO1: Acquire knowledge of various business disciplines including human resource management, accounting, marketing, finance, supply chain management, business statistics, business law & ethics, business research and related disciplines.
PLO2: Use analytical and reflective thinking techniques to identify and analyze problems, develop viable alternatives, and make effective decisions and be able to implement appropriate qualitative and quantitative techniques in solving business cases and analyzing financial statements.
PLO3: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern methods with an understanding of the limitations and their usage.
PLO4: Apply the knowledge in the field of research to generate new concepts and business ideas.
PLO5: Demonstrate effective application of modern technologies in the field of business.
PLO6: Gain expertise the business field and will be able to develop as the type of managers the modern organizations need or expose as entrepreneurs with innovative business ideas.
PLO7: Discern the need for continuous professional development in a competitive environment to meet challenges of the society and contribute to the protection and development of the society with their business expertise in the long run.
PLO8: Identify and analyze ethical and legal conflicts and social responsibility issues and comply with ethical, professional, regulatory, environmental and socially responsible organizational policies and practices.
PLO9: Develop professionalism to function effectively as an individual, as a member or leader in diverse teams and as a multidisciplinary person in every context.
PLO10: Articulate themselves as effective communicator through writing effective business documents, preparing and delivering presentations and developing appropriate interpersonal skills.
PLO11: Manage and use the resources in various business aspects such as managing inventory, raw materials sourcing, distribution management, marketing campaigns, financial planning and so on.
PLO12: Engage in independent and lifelong learning in the wider context of technological changes.

Master of Business Administration (Regular) Program

1. Program Educational Objectives (PEO):
PEO Descriptions
---
PEO1: To deliver high quality education to the students of business at an affordable price.
PEO2: To ensure students gain fundamental, technical and advanced knowledge in different fields of business so that they can get accustomed with the local and global environmental conditions.
PEO3: To enhance the link between teaching & learning and promote effective research in various business disciplines.
PEO4: To provide an educational environment which is collaborative that students can engage in personal and professional developments such as leadership, entrepreneurship, innovation, self-motivation, self-awareness and effective communication skills while gaining theoretical and practical skills, which can be implemented in real work scenarios by the corporate executives.
PEO5: To build strong standards of ethics in students by teaching them about integrity, morality, honesty etc. through different academic programs, seminars and symposiums in order to improve the society.
PEO6: To provide training to the students about developing life-long learning by finding out innovation in business opportunities and formulating strategies to meet the needs of a dynamic business environment.

2. Program Learning Outcomes (PLO):
After completion Master of Business Administration (Regular) Program, the students will be able to obtain the following things:

PLO Descriptions
---
PLO1: Applied Business Knowledge: The students will develop practical knowledge on various business areas such as Human Resource Management, Accounting, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Business Statistics, Business Law & Ethics, Business Research etc.
PLO2: Problem Exploration: The students will make themselves able to apply analytical and insightful thinking techniques to identify and analyze problems, develop feasible alternatives, and make effective decisions.
PLO3: Problem Solving Skill: The students will make themselves able to create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern methods with an understanding of the limitations and its usage.
PLO4: Knowledge, Skills and Attitudes (KSAs) for Research: The students will be able to develop required KSAs in the field of research to generate new concepts and business ideas and modify the current concepts and ideas.
PLO5: Modern Tools Usage: The students will be able to demonstrate effective application of modern technologies in the field of business.
PLO6: Business Graduates and Global Village: The students will develop expertise in the business field and will develop themselves as efficient managers and entrepreneurs for the global village.
PLO7: Environment and Sustainability: The students will be able to understand the need for continuous professional development in a competitive environment to meet challenges of the society and contribute to the protection and development of the society with their business expertise in the long-run.
PLO8: Ethics: The students will be able to identify, analyze ethical conflicts and social responsibility issues and comply with ethical, professional, regulatory, environmental and socially responsible organizational policies and practices.
PLO9: Individual Work and Teamwork: The students will be able to develop professionalism to function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams' acts as a multidisciplinary person in every context.
PLO10: Total Communication Package (TCP): The students will develop an excellent TCP through writing effective business documents, public speaking, presentation and developing appropriate interpersonal skills.
PLO11: Managing Resources: The students will be able to manage and use the resources in various business aspects such as managing human resources, managing inventory, raw materials sourcing, distribution management, marketing campaigns, financial planning and so on.
PLO12: Lifelong Learning: The students will be able to engage in independent and lifelong learning in the broadest context of technological change.

Biography
Short Bio of Professor Dr. Farhana Helal Mehtab
Professor Dr. Farhana Helal Mehtab is a distinguished legal academic and the first female Dean of the Faculty of Law of private universities in Bangladesh. She joined Southeast University (SEU) as Dean of the School of Arts & Social Sciences and was appointed Dean of the School of Law. Dr. Mehtab has over two decades of leadership experience in higher education. She previously served as Dean of the Faculty of Law and the Faculty of Arts & Social Sciences at the Green University of Bangladesh (GUB) and, before that, as Head/ Chairperson of the Department of Law at Daffodil International University (DIU). Leading departments at three different universities consecutively has established her as a highly accomplished academic administrator. She is also a Visiting Faculty member at Chandigarh University, India, and an Academic Council Member at the Bangladesh Army International University of Science & Technology (BAIUST). Dr. Mehtab earned her PhD, LLM, and LLB (Honors) from the University of Dhaka. She received a Master of Education degree from the Institute of Education and Research (IER), DU. Combining her core subjects, i.e., Law and Education, she received her PhD in "Constitutional Responsibility of the Government of Bangladesh for Implementing Compulsory Primary Education: Issues & Challenges" Her teaching and research areas include Human Rights Law, Humanitarian Law, Gender and the Law, Good Governance, International Environmental Law, Criminology, Legal Research Methodology. Dr. Mehtab is the author of four Legal books on Terrorism and Counterterrorism, Human Trafficking International & Bangladesh Perspective, Legal English, and Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) in Bangladesh. She received professional training in collaborative arbitration from the Bangladesh International Arbitration Centre (BIAC) and the International Law Institute (ILI), Washington D.C. She was awarded the International Academy of the Belt and Road Fellowship in 2016, Hong Kong. She is a member of the Asian Association of Law Professors (AALP) and serves on the International Advisory Board of the International Academy of the Belt and Road, China. Recently she has become the Advisory Board member of the South Asia Chapter of the Women's Network of Gender Champions against Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling (the original chapter of the Women's Network was constituted by UNODC in June 2020). She was a Syndicate member in DIU & GUB. Currently, she is a Syndicate member of SEU.

Biography
Md. Asraful Islam is an esteemed academic and legal researcher, currently serving as Assistant Professor and Chairman in the Department of Law at Southeast University, Bangladesh, and as a PhD Research Fellow at the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM). With over 19 years of experience in legal education and research, he has held several prominent academic roles, including Director of the Center for Legal Research and Chairman of the Department of Law at Southeast University. Mr. Islam holds an LLB (Hons) and an LLM from the University of Rajshahi, graduating with first-class honors, and was awarded the IIUM Khair Award PhD Scholarship for his ongoing doctoral research. Mr. Islam's expertise spans diverse areas of law, including international human rights, the Bangladesh legal system, media and information technology law, international commercial arbitration, access to justice, and legal aid. His contributions to legal scholarship are extensive, with numerous peer-reviewed articles published in esteemed journals on topics such as child rights, intellectual property, public interest litigation, and maritime law. He has also supported the Bangladesh government as a legal translator, working on legislative documents for the Ministry Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs. In addition to his research and publications, Islam is an active participant in national and international conferences, where he has presented on issues such as religious diversity in the workplace and the potential for public interest litigation in Bangladesh. His professional training includes workshops and seminars hosted by institutions like the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and the National Human Rights Commission of Bangladesh (NHRC). Fluent in both Bangla and English, Islam is also proficient in various digital tools, enhancing his research and teaching capabilities. Throughout his career, Islam has received numerous awards and scholarships, including early academic scholarships, merit-based university awards for his LLB and LLM achievements, and research grants from prestigious institutions. As an enrolled advocate with the Bangladesh Bar Council and an active member of the Rajshahi University Law Alumni Association, he remains deeply connected to both academic and professional legal communities. His dedication to advancing legal research and education underscores his ongoing commitment promoting justice, human rights, and progressive legal frameworks in Bangladesh and beyond.

Biography
MOHAMMAD JAHID MUSTOFA is a distinguished academician and legal professional in Bangladesh. He is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Law, Southeast University (SEU). Academic Background: Md. Jahid Mustofa has an excellent academic record from secondary to postgraduate levels. He completed his Secondary School Certificate (SSC) in Science with First Division, earning a Board Scholarship. He then completed his Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) in Science with First Division and a Board Scholarship. He obtained his Bachelor of Laws (LL.B. Honours) from the Faculty of Law, University of Dhaka, securing 3rd merit position and a University Scholarship. He subsequently completed his Master of Laws (LL.M.) from the same faculty, achieving 5th merit position, and a University Scholarship. He is currently pursuing a PhD in Law at the University of Rajshahi. Teaching Experience: Md. Jahid Mustofa has over 13 years of full-time university-level teaching experience. At Southeast University, he has served as Assistant Professor, Senior Lecturer, and Lecturer. Prior to joining SEU, he worked as a Lecturer at Prime University and the University of Development Alternative (UODA). Administrative and Non-Teaching Experience: Alongside teaching, Md. Jahid Mustofa has made extensive contributions to university administration. He has served as Chairman, Department of Law, Southeast University. His other key roles include Academic Coordinator (LLB & LLM Programs), Member and Ex-Member of IQAC, Member, Self-Assessment Committee (SAC) and Head of SAC, Member Secretary, Proctorial Committee, Member Secretary, Complaint Committee to Prevent and Redress Sexual Harassment, and Member Secretary and Member of various Ad hoc Fact-Finding and Investigation Committees. Research and Publications: Md. Jahid Mustofa is an active researcher with 14 peer-reviewed journal publications in national and international journals, covering diverse areas such as environmental law, constitutional law, consumer protection, human rights, climate justice, information privacy, and criminal justice. Professional Qualification: Md. Jahid Mustofa is an enrolled Advocate of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, having completed professional legal training from the Legal Education and Training Institute (LETI), Bangladesh Bar Council.

clean_text: About Vision Mission Department of Pharmacy PEOs and POs Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) Upon completing B. Pharm program at Department of Pharmacy, SEU the undergraduate students will be able to - PEO Descriptions --- --- PEO1: Possess fundamental, technical and advanced knowledge in the various fields of health and pharmaceutical sciences to pursue higher studies. PEO2: Demonstrate essential technical and research skills that make them confident to create new knowledge and analyze, identify, formulate and solve issues associated with pharmaceutical industry and/or research institutes at home and abroad. PEO3: Engage and flourish in their professional careers through innovation, team work, entrepreneurship, good communication skills and proactive involvement to contribute functional expertise on interdisciplinary teams creating solutions to complex problems. PEO4: Exhibit professional ethics, responsibilities and norms of the pharmacy practices to assume leading managerial roles in their organizations and professional communities. PEO5: Reveal the importance of lifelong learning to cope up with the advancements in different areas of health and pharmaceutical sciences and continuous professional development to meet challenges for discharging professional responsibilities to ensure quality life. Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs) After completion of four-year B. Pharm program, the students will be able to- PLO Descriptions --- --- PLO1: Demonstrate the fundamental knowledge of pharmacology, pharmaceutical technology and engineering, dosage form designing, pharmacognosy, physiology and anatomy, pharmaceutical chemistry, clinical and hospital pharmacy, pharmaceutical management, regulatory affairs, biostatistics and mathematics and specialization of complex clinical and pharmaceutical problems. PLO2: Identify, formulate, investigate and analyze complex problems regarding formulation development, quality control and quality assurance, drug use management, biomedical research and reach sustained conclusion using the principles chemistry, medicine, mathematics and pharmacy sciences. PLO3: Design effective solutions for complex pharmaceutical technology, engineering and drug quality control, drug designing related problems and design system components or processes of pharmaceutical industry, research laboratories that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for biohazard and safety. PLO4: Conduct investigations in various scientific fields comprising pharmaceutical technology, pharmacology, natural product chemistry and biomedical areas using experimental design, data analysis and interpretation, and information synthesis to provide valid conclusions create new knowledge. PLO5: Select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and operate various modern scientific instruments used in pharmaceutical experiments, drug manufacturing machines, and different kinds of drug designing, and analytical software. PLO6: Exhibit reasoning using contextual knowledge to assess societal, public health, drug safety, drug dispensing and distribution, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to professional pharmacy practices. PLO7: Demonstrate the impact of professional pharmacy solutions in societal and environmental contexts and demonstrate the knowledge of and need for sustainable development to meet the new challenges in health and pharmaceutical areas. PLO8: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, responsibilities and norms of pharmacy practices. PLO9: Function effectively as an individual and as a member or leader of diverse teams in multidisciplinary settings of pharmaceutical and other relevant fields. PLO10: Communicate effectively about complex pharmaceutical concepts and issues to pharmacy community, other healthcare professionals and society at large. PLO11: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of pharmaceutical science and management principles and apply these to one's work as a team member or a leader to manage projects utilizing physical and human resources in multidisciplinary environment such as healthcare institutes, research institutes, industry etc. PLO12: Identify the need for the preparation to engage in independent, life-long learning in the broadest context of new advancements in health and pharmaceutical sciences. Prof. Dr. Md. Selim Reza Adviser & Professor Room: 706, 7th Floor selimreza@seu.edu.bd Biography Dr. Md. Selim Reza is a Grade-1 Professor in the Department of Pharmaceutical Technology at the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Dhaka. He served as Chair of the department from 2014 to 2017 and has held several academic leadership positions, including Acting Head at the University of Asia Pacific (2003–2006) and Southeast University (2008–2011), and Adviser at Daffodil International University (2013–2016). He completed his B. Pharm (Hons.) and M. Pharm degrees from the University of Dhaka in 1987 and 1989, respectively. He earned his PhD in Pharmaceutical Technology from the University of Strathclyde, UK, in 1997 under the Commonwealth Scholarship, where his research focused on biodegradable microspheres for drug delivery. In 2003, he received a Commonwealth postdoctoral fellowship at King's College London, conducting research on microencapsulation for pulmonary drug delivery. Dr. Reza has contributed extensively to regulatory and quality systems in Bangladesh. He served as a member of the Drug Control Subcommittee of the Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA) from 2014 to 2017 and participated in evaluating DGDA's Quality Management System in line with ISO 9001:2015 and WHO Global Benchmarking Tool standards. He also worked as a World Bank consultant with the Ministry Health and Family Welfare (2017–2022) for the implementation of the 4th Health, Population and Nutrition Sector Programme (4th HPNSP). In addition, he served as Head of the Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) of the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Dhaka, promoting Outcome-Based Education (OBE). He has also been a member of a Supreme Court–appointed inspection team that assessed pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities in Bangladesh regarding GMP compliance and regulatory standards. Dr. Abul Hasanat Alamgir Director, IRT & Professor Room: 506, 5th Floor director.irt@seu.edu.bd, h.alamgir@seu.edu.bd Biography Prof. Dr. Hasnat M Alamgir is a Professor in the Pharmacy department and Director of Research and Training. Professor Alamgir completed PhD in Epidemiology from the University of British Columbia, Canada. worked before as a research scientist in Canada and as university faculty in the United States, received research grants from several organizations in Canada and USA, mentored master's and doctoral students, and published more than 75 research papers in international journals. He is a newspaper columnist on public health issues. title: Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
clean_text:
Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)
After 3 to 5 years of completion of Bachelor of Information & Communication Technology program, the graduates would be able (to show the following qualities):

PEO Description
---
PEO1 To prepare students to apply core knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and specialized ICT principles to analyze and solve complex technological, communication, and information-centric problems.

PEO2 To prepare students for lifelong learning, professional employment, and advanced studies by providing substantial exposure to modern ICT systems, digital infrastructures, communication technologies, data-driven solutions, and emerging innovations necessary for real-world applications.

PEO3 To develop effective teamwork, communication, and interpersonal skills so that graduates can work collaboratively in multidisciplinary and multicultural environments within the ICT profession.

PEO4 To foster ethical, responsible, and socially conscious professionals who understand ICT-related legal, global, environmental, security, and societal implications.

Program Learning Outcomes
Upon successful completion of Bachelor of Science in Information & Communication Technology program the students will be able to obtain the following knowledge and skills:

PLO Description
---
PO1 Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop solutions of complex engineering problems.

PO2 Identify, formulate, research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences and engineering sciences with holistic considerations for sustainable development (WK1 to WK4).

PO3 Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design systems, components or processes to meet identified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon as well as resource, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations as

PO4 Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research methods including research-based knowledge, design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions (WK8).

PO5 Create, select and apply and recognize limitations of appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modeling, to complex engineering problems (WK2, WK6).

PO6 When solving complex engineering problems, analyze and evaluate sustainable development impacts to: society, the economy, sustainability, health and safety, legal frameworks, and the environment (WK1, WK5, and WK7).

PO7 Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and norms of engineering practice and adhere to relevant national and international laws. Demonstrate an understanding of the need for diversity and inclusion (WK9).

PO8 Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader diverse and inclusive teams and in multi-disciplinary, face-to-face, remote and distributed settings (WK9).

PO9 Communicate effectively and inclusively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, taking into account cultural, language, and learning differences.

PO10 Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO11 Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change (WK8).

PO12 Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the competences necessary to transform opportunities and ideas into a new business.

title: Iqac Vision
clean_text: To build a world-class educational ecosystem that nurtures innovative and ethically grounded leaders, equipping them to drive sustainable development. Through academic excellence, cutting-edge research, and strong institutional governance, we empower individuals to create meaningful societal impact and contribute to global progress.

title: Mission
clean_text:
Mission
M1: To provide transformative, high-quality education that inspires lifelong learning and advances a sustainable, knowledge-driven society. We achieve academic excellence by combining rigorous standards, innovative pedagogy, and cutting-edge research to empower learners and shape the future.
M2: Foster a culture of collaborative research and innovation through strong national and global partnerships. push the frontiers of knowledge and drive meaningful societal impact with transformative discoveries.
M3: Cultivate an educational ecosystem rooted in excellence, inclusivity, and transparency. Through rigorous quality assurance, we continuously elevate teaching, curriculum, and institutional accountability to empower learners and uphold the highest standards.
M4: Partner with local, national, and global communities to position the university as a catalyst for societal progress. We cultivate collaborations that advance equity, justice, diversity, and sustainability—driving meaningful change at every level.
M5: Empower students to emerge as principled leaders and engaged global citizens, equipped to address society's greatest challenges. We instill integrity, empathy, and social responsibility—preparing them to navigate complexity and drive positive change in an interconnected world.
M6: Champion Bangladesh's vibrant cultural heritage while cultivating a global outlook that connects students worldwide academic and cultural communities. We nurture both deep national pride and a forward-thinking awareness of global challenges and possibilities.
M7: Drive educational excellence through continuous innovation—adopting global best practices, refreshing curricula, and investing in faculty growth. We prioritize student-centered learning and critical thinking to empower graduates with both academic mastery and professional success.

Quality Assurance Committee (QAC)

The committee set up by the university authority for institutional oversight of the IQAC. In order to look after the key issues of quality assurance and activities of the IQAC the Quality Assurance Committee (QAC) has been constituted in Southeast University (SEU). The IQAC shall report to the Vice Chancellor (VC) and be supervised by the University's QAC.

Functions of QAC:
1. The QAC shall be an advisory body to the IQAC for developing an effective and workable system of quality assurance.
2. QAC shall act as a planning forum for the discussion and promotion of the developments in quality assurance culture.

Job Description of Director, IQAC
1. Oversee the management of IQAC and be responsible for all its activities;
2. Establish milestones and performance indicators for smooth and effective implementation of IQAC activities to meet the international standards;
3. Take necessary steps to develop a culture with a view to achieving position in World University Rankings;
4. Work as the Chief Liaison Officer (CLO) among the UGC, the respective universities and the QAU;
5. Co-ordinate, supervise and monitor all QA and TL related activities of the IQAC within the university;
6. Establish a liaison with other universities and research organizations at home and abroad to learn the best practices;
7. Explore the emerging issues with regard to higher education and recommend those to the QAC and the UGC;
8. Prepare performance-based budget subject to availability of grants, aid, endowment from the UGC and other organizations;
9. Arrange meetings on a regular basis to assess the performance of the IQAC in promoting the best QA culture and TL practices within the university;
10. Formulate strategic plan and recommend it to the QAC and the UGC for enhancement of overall quality of the university;
11. Develop a data-base software of information regarding the training to be delivered to all relevant stakeholders on QA and TL;
12. Execute all QA and TL related decisions as directed by the UGC, the QAC and Syndicate/Regent Board of the university;
13. Report to the QAC and the UGC twice a year.

Job Description of Additional Director (Quality Assurance-QA)
1. Assist in formulating policies for different QA aspects of the university relating to governance, leadership strengthening, curriculum development, faculty and professional staff development.
2. Play a key role in monitoring, evaluation, and continual improvement of QA.
3. Collect data/ evidence on the implementation of the policies formulated and prepare a report on all QA related activities.
4. Develop an improvement plan regarding QA for every 4 years and ensure its effective implementation and monitoring.
5. Assist POEs and the university in culturing the procedures for accreditation of the programs and university as per the guidelines set by the BAC.
6. Execute QA related decisions as directed by the UGC and/or by the QAC and Syndicate/Regent Board of the university.
7. Facilitate the self-assessment and external peer review conducted by the PSAC.
8. Implement the QA process at program level.
9. Assist in developing an online data-base software enriched with all information regarding the QA activities and monitoring and evaluating those.
10. Conduct annual academic audit at every POE level.

Job Description of Additional Director (Excellence in Teaching Learning-ETL)
1. Plan training/workshop/seminar etc. for faculties, officers, and support staff to implement policies regarding all aspects of teaching-learning.
2. Review the literature related to modernization of curriculum, teaching-leaning, and research etc.
3. Conduct research on various aspects of teaching-learning, performance of teachers, students' leaning behavior, blended leaning mode, code of conduct for teachers and students, and so on.
4. Conduct research on the implementation of outcome-based teaching-learning and assessment.
5. Assist the university authority to introduce an award recognition system for excellence in teaching-learning, research, leadership quality, office management skills, etc.
6. Respond to the requests regarding training, and formulate training proposals, deliver courses, prepare necessary documents, etc.
7. Identify and organize short training courses on professional development.
8. Guide and assist the POEs of the university to implement the Outcome Based Education (OBE).
9. Develop an improvement plan regarding ETL for every 4 years and ensure its effective implementation as well as monitoring of its achievements.
10. Assist in developing data-based software containing all information on the programs undertaken for ETL.
11. Execute ETL related decisions as directed by the UGC and/or by the QAC and Syndicate/Regent Board of the respective university.
12. Provide training to the faculty members to implement research and scholarly activities.

title: Journal of Architecture
clean_text:
Journal of Architecture

Guidelines for Authors for Southeast University Journal Of Architecture (SEUJA)

Business Contact

Manuscript Organization

Running Head
Running head should be added in the Header along with the page numbers.
Characters: Up to 50
Font: Cambria (Headings)
Size: 12
Alignment: Left

Type of Article
Research Article/ Case Report/ Review Article/ Opinion/ Short Communication/ Mini Review/ Letter to Editor

Title
The title of the paper should provide a concise statement of the contents of the paper. A good title is very important and will attract readers and facilitate retrieval by online searches, thereby helping to maximize citations. The title should include topical keywords and allude to the interesting conclusions of the paper. A title that emphasizes the main conclusions, or poses a question, has more impact than one that just describes the nature of the study.

Running Title
A short 'running title', of not more than 55 characters (including spaces), for use as a headline.
Words: Up to 20.
Font: Cambria (Headings)
Size: 12.
Alignment: Center
Title should be in Bold and in Title Case.

Authors and affiliations
Author names should be given in upper- and lower-case, not in all capitals, to avoid ambiguities. The author for correspondence must be clearly indicated. It is permissible to include the names of more than one author as the corresponding author, but a single author must act as the point of communication during the peer review process.
The name and address of the laboratory or laboratories and university where the work was done, and present addresses of authors who have since moved.

Corresponding author details
Detailed Author's address, including telephone number, Fax number and email address for the corresponding author should be mentioned.

Abstract
Abstract should include a brief content of the article. Please minimize the use abbreviations and do not cite references in the abstract. This should state the objectives of the work, but should not contain a detailed summary of the results.
Words: Up to 250
Font: Cambria
Size: 10

Keywords
Select keywords that will make your manuscript easily searchable. Three to ten keywords representing the main content of the article.
Words: Up to 10
Font: Cambria
Size: 10

Abbreviations
Please include any non-standard abbreviations referred to within your paper. A list of standard abbreviations can be found here.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10

Introduction
This outlines the state of current research and the context of the research presented. Often it will cover work previously carried out by the same research team and how the new results relate to that. Because the introduction states a lot of background material and little to no original research, it usual contains the bulk of the citations - often to larger "review" papers.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Material and Methods
The experimental section covers materials, methods and explains the procedures used in the paper. This is often full of technical detail, precise spectrometer frequencies, equipment specifications or the origin of materials. Due to the technical nature of these sections, they are sometimes pushed to the back, or rendered in a smaller font, or perhaps moved to the supplementary materials.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Results
In a self-explanatory manner, states the results of experiments or work carried out. Depending on the nature of the work, results may be mixed in with discussion. Results sections can also be split into several parts forming distinct parts of a paper. For example, one section may discuss experimental findings while another looks at computer models to support this.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Discussion
This should not recapitulate the results, and should not be too long. Discussion must illustrate and interpret the report of the study. It may be helpful to list the main conclusions at the end. A combined Results and Discussion section is encouraged where appropriate.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Conclusion
This section towards the end of the paper further summaries the important results and implications.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Acknowledgements
An Acknowledgements section is not compulsory but may be included. If required, Provide list of individuals who contributed in the work and grant details other than main authors. Authors may also wish to acknowledge individuals who have contributed materials, expertise or time to the study who are not named as authors.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

Conflict of Interest
Declare if any economic interest or any conflict of interest exists.

If there are any sub headings in the body text, sub-categorize them accordingly under the heading in which they fall.
For example:
1. Heading
1.1. Sub-heading
1.1.1. Sub-sub-heading
Font: Cambria
Size: 10

References
Throughout the paper, any statement will be backed up with notes to additional literature. These are stated in a reference section in numbered order of citation in the text towards the end of the paper. Reference shall be organized in APA of Harvard Style. List all authors if less than six. If more than five authors, list the first five followed by "et.al." Provide the link for the listed references.
Font: Cambria
Size: 10.

title: Southeast University Ranks 1St In Innovation And 2Nd Overall In Bangladesh Scimago 2026 R
clean_text: Southeast University Ranks 1st in Innovation and 2nd Overall in Bangladesh: Scimago 2026 Rankings Southeast University has secured the 2nd position in Overall Ranking and the top position in the Innovation category among Bangladeshi universities, according to the 2026 rankings released by Spain's renowned education and research organization, Scimago. In its latest report covering 10,827 universities across the globe, Scimago Institutions Ranking's country-wise data reveal that Southeast University has surpassed other prestigious universities in Bangladesh to claim the first position in the Innovation category. This milestone highlights the university's growing social and academic impact and recognition as a major knowledge hub. Southeast solidifies its position as a center of educational excellence in the country and affirms its commitment to providing high-quality education.

title: Southeast University Pays Tribute To Language Martyrs On Intl Mother Language Day
clean_text:
Southeast University (SEU) solemnly observed the Great Shaheed Day and International Mother Language Day in remembrance of the martyrs of the historic Language Movement of 1952. The university organized a Provat Feri (mourning procession), a discussion session, and a cultural program to pay tribute to the language heroes. The Provat Feri commenced from the university campus gate and paraded through various roads of Tejgaon before concluding at the Shaheed Minar established on the SEU campus. Floral wreaths were placed at the administrative officials, and students.

In the discussion session, the Honorable Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, delivered his speech highlighting the significance of the Language Movement in the emergence of Bangladesh. The Pro-Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. M. Mofazzal Hossain, the Registrar, Major General Md. Anwarul Islam, SUP, ndu, psc (Retd.), and the Convener of the program and Head of the Department of Architecture, Dr. Masud Ur Rashid, also addressed the audience. The speakers emphasized the importance of the 1952 Language Movement in shaping the nation and urged the younger generation to learn the true history of the country and be inspired by the spirit of patriotism.

The cultural segment featured drama, recitation, dance, and musical performances presented by members of various clubs of Southeast University. Deans of different faculties, department heads, faculty members, club representatives, officials, staff, and students were present at the event.

title: The Department of Economics, SEU Signs MoU with Dnet for Academic and Research Collaboration
clean_text:
The Department of Economics, SEU Signs MoU with Dnet for Academic and Research Collaboration

The Department of Economics at Southeast University signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Dnet to foster joint academic and research initiatives. The signing ceremony took place at SEU and was attended by Professor Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, PhD, Honorable Vice Chancellor, SEU; Professor Dr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro Vice-Chancellor; SEU, Professor Dr. Farhana Helal Mehtab, Dean of the School of Arts and Social Sciences; SEU, Mr. Md. Tarik Al Jalil, Secretary, BOT, SEUT and Mahmudul Hasan, Executive Director of Dnet. All dignitaries emphasized the importance of industry-university collaboration in the area of academic and research. This partnership marks a significant step as SEU's Economics Department builds formal academic ties with a reputed research organization, creating opportunities for joint research and capacity-building programs. Faculty members from the Department of Economics, SEU actively participated in the event, reflecting a strong commitment to interdisciplinary academic engagement.

title: Southeast University Signs Mou With The British Council
clean_text: Southeast University has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the British Council to strengthen academic collaboration and enhance initiatives in English language education and assessment. The MoU Signing Ceremony was held at the university campus in the presence of senior officials from both institutions. The Honorable Vice Chancellor of Southeast University, Professor Dr. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, and Mr. Maxim Raimann, Country Exams Director of the British Council, expressed optimism regarding the scope and sustainability of the collaboration. The event was also attended by Professor Dr. M. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro-Vice Chancellor of Southeast University; Maj Gen Md Anwarul Islam, SUP, ndu, psc (Retd.), Registrar of SEU; Professor Dr. Farhana Helal Mehtab, Dean, School of Law and School of Arts & Social Sciences; Dr. Zaheed Alam Munna, Chairman, Department of English; and Dr. Muhammad Tofazzal Hossain, Convener of the MoU Committee, along with faculty members and officials of the university. The partnership aims to promote excellence in English language teaching and learning, professional development, assessment support, and capacity-building programs for both students and faculty members. This collaboration reflects Southeast University's continued commitment to academic quality, international engagement, and alignment with global standards in higher education. title: Young Economists Of Seu Successfully Organized Enact
clean_text: Young Economists of SEU (YES) organized ENACT, an event that brought together students from different institutions to engage in academic competition and policy-oriented discussion. The program featured a Quiz Competition and a Policy Case Tournament, designed to encourage analytical thinking, economic reasoning, and practical policy analysis among participants. ENACT was presented by Synergy Solution and powered by Super Star Group Limited, whose support contributed significantly to the smooth execution of the event. The program was honored by the presence of Nazme Sabina, Chief Executive of DevResonance Ltd., as the Chief Guest. In her address, she emphasized the importance of developing critical thinking and policy analysis skills among young learners to prepare them for future professional and leadership roles. The judging panel consisted of Professor Md Nazmus Sadekin, Dean of the Faculty of Social Science and Chairman of the Department of Economics at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University; Dr. Wasim Akram, Assistant Professor, Department of Economics, Southeast University; Md. Abul Hasan Chowdhury, Deputy Director (Statistics) at Bangladesh Bank; and Enamul Hafiz Latifee, Chief Research Officer of Textile Today. As the first inter-university initiative of Young Economists of SEU (YES), ENACT successfully created a platform for academic engagement, healthy competition, and policy-based learning.

clean_text: A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between Southeast University (SEU) and the Amanat Shah Group at the university's Multipurpose Hall. Strategic directives were issued to bolster academic quality, strengthen research capabilities, and improve operational efficiency. The Board further emphasized the importance of expanding industry collaborations, integrating cutting-edge technologies, and pursuing sustainable institutional growth. title: Southeast University Achieves Historic Debut In Qs Asia University Rankings
clean_text: Southeast University Achieves Historic Debut in QS Asia University Rankings. The university celebrated this significant milestone with a special meeting held in the Conference Room. The meeting was chaired by the Pro Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Dr. M. Mofazzal Hossain. He shared the university's outstanding specific achievements: 9th among Private Universities, 23rd among All Universities in Bangladesh, 224th in Southern Asia, Ranked within the 741-750 band in Asia. Professor Mofazzal Hossain extended his deepest gratitude to all faculty and staff for their "tremendous hard work and unwavering dedication", which pivotal in securing this global recognition. He stated, "This amazing achievement marks SEU's step onto the global stage...these specific rankings—9th among private universities in Bangladesh and our solid placement in Asia—are a clear reflection of our collective commitment to quality... Every member of our community deserves heartfelt thanks for making this debut possible". He concluded by stressing the importance of continuous improvement to achieve even better rank in future editions of QS, THE, and other international systems, with the goal of elevating SEU's standing as a leading institution. The meeting was attended by the Registrar, Deans, Heads of the department, Professors and Senior officials.

title: Southeast University Mourns The Passing Of Nuclear Scientist Dr M Shamsher Ali
clean_text: Dr. M. Shamsher Southeast University Mourns the Passing of Nuclear Scientist Dr. M. Shamsher Ali On behalf of the Southeast University Board of Trustees, Board Chairman Mr. Rezaul Karim, along with Southeast University's Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam and Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. M. Mofazzal Hossain, have expressed profound condolences to the bereaved family of the late Professor Dr. M. Shamsher Ali. Dr. Ali, a distinguished nuclear scientist and renowned educator, was also the founding Vice-Chancellor of Southeast University. They prayed for the salvation of his departed soul. Professor Dr. M. Shamsher Ali served as the founding Vice-Chancellor of Southeast University when it was established in 2002. His life was dedicated to advancing science, education, and human knowledge and was marked by extraordinary success. Dr. Ali was a respected scholar who made significant contributions to the field of nuclear physics, with numerous research papers published in international journals. His academic career was highly decorated; he received both the Hari Prasanna Roy Gold Medal and the Bangladesh Academy of Sciences Gold Medal. As the founding Vice-Chancellor of both Bangladesh Open University and Southeast University, he played a crucial role in the development of higher education and its institutions in Bangladesh. He was deeply passionate about popularizing science, an interest he reflected through his writings on the synthesis of science and culture and his countless discussions on radio and television. His work on the relationship between science and religion and on interfaith harmony demonstrated his deep concern for global peace and harmony. His legacy will live on through the countless students, teachers, and alumni whose lives were shaped by his vision and commitment to excellence in education.

title: IRT of Southeast University Holds a Talk on the Impact of Climate Change
clean_text:
IRT of Southeast University Holds a Talk on the Impact of Climate Change

Professor Ainun Nishat from Southeast University (SEU) spoke about the impact of climate change and the need for sustainable development. The event was inaugurated by the Pro Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Dr. M. Mofazzal Hossain, while the IRT Director, Prof. Dr. Abul Hasanat Alamgir, moderated it.

Professor Ainun Nishat emphasized that preserving ecosystems such as rivers, forests, and wetlands is crucial for maintaining a healthy environment and supporting people's lives and livelihoods. He stated, "Sustainable development means finding a balance between growing the economy, helping people, and protecting the environment." He also highlighted that universities play a significant role in promoting sustainability by educating students, researching clean energy and climate solutions, adopting eco-friendly campus practices, and engaging with communities on projects such as tree planting and water conservation.

Dr. Nishat warned that if climate change continues at its current rate, Bangladesh will face critical challenges, including rising sea levels, unpredictable and extreme weather, food shortages, and displacement of people. He urged immediate and responsible action to secure a safe and sustainable future.

This insightful discussion was organized by the Institute of Research and Training (IRT) at Southeast University.

title: Professor Meer Mobashsher Ali Former Head Of The Department Of Architecture Passes Away
clean_text: It is with profound sadness that we announce the demise Professor Meer Mobashsher Ali, founding head of the Department of Architecture at Southeast University. Professor Ali was a distinguished architect and educator, whose contributions have left an indelible mark on architectural education in Bangladesh. He began his long-standing association with BUET's Department of Architecture, dedicating over four decades to teaching and mentoring. The Department of Architecture at Southeast University embarked on its journey in October 2010 under the visionary leadership of Professor Meer Mobashsher Ali. His dedication and guidance played a pivotal role in shaping the department, laying a strong foundation for its growth and excellence. Throughout his tenure, Professor Ali held various pivotal roles, including Department Head and Dean of the Faculty. He was instrumental in shaping the curriculum and fostering an environment that emphasized creativity and innovation in architectural education. Professor Meer Mobashsher Ali's dedication to education and his passion for architecture will be remembered and cherished by all who had the privilege of knowing him.

clean_text: Robotics – The Southeast Computer Club Hosts Seminar on "Introduction to Robotics – The Ultimate Roadmap" Southeast Computer Club (SEUCC) held an engaging seminar titled "Introduction to Robotics – The Ultimate Roadmap" at Shaheed Rakib Hall, Southeast University. A special moment was when Mr. Mohammad Nazmuddoza, Director of Career & Professional Development Services (CPDS), shared a brief yet inspiring speech, expressing his gratitude to everyone involved in organizing the seminar and underscoring the significance of such events in nurturing future professionals in the robotics field. The seminar was chaired by Mr. Shifat Ahmed, Assistant Professor and Coordinator, Department of CSE, who graciously stepped in for Mr. Shahriar Manzoor, Associate Professor and Chairman of the Department of CSE, in his absence. title: About SEU
clean_text:
About SEU
Situated in a centrally located vertical campus in Tejgaon, Dhaka, Southeast University (SEU) has 10 departments and houses more than 12000 students under three schools, School of Science and Engineering (SSE), Southeast Business School (SBS), and School of Arts and Social Sciences (SASS). Having started its journey in 2002, SEU is poised to establish itself as one of the leading private universities in Bangladesh. Given its motto, "Meeting the challenges of Time" the university is always introducing new programs and soft-skill development initiatives. The university aims to provide up-to-date education, hands-on application, and research facilities to its students. SEU has always strived to provide higher education at an affordable cost, considering the economic conditions of the middle and lowermiddle-income families in Bangladesh. SEU aims to impart worldclass education and help students reach their highest capacities. SEU has implemented the global curriculum for all programs and updates the syllabus based on the changing tides. SEU believes excellence can only be earned through hard work and perseverance. Therefore, the hope to transform students into hardworking and ethical humans who can contribute positively to the society.

title: Seu Architecture Students Showcase Design Projects On Minimalistic Shelter For
clean_text: Students of 2nd Year, 3rd Semester, (Batch 38,39) showcased their creativity and innovation through 12 group design projects under the theme Project Sanctuary: A Minimalistic Shelter for the Rohingya Community. The works were exhibited in poster format at the prestigious 4th Border Urbanism Conference 2025 in Graz, Austria, drawing global attention to sustainable, humane, and community-centered design solutions. Adding to this milestone, the projects are also in progress for publication as chapters in The Routledge Handbook of Border Urbanism Discourse (Taylor & Francis, Routledge), a major academic volume addressing migration, displacement, and shelter design. This remarkable journey was made possible through the overall coordination of Dr. Quazi Mahtab Zaman, PhD (Architecture & Urbanism), Scott Sutherland School of Architecture & Built Environment, Robert Gordon University; under the supervision of Ar. Syed Monirul Islam, Associate Professor, Department of Architecture, SEU and with the dedicated guidance of studio mentors Khairun Nahar, Kowshik Ahmed, and Shariar Alam Santo. We congratulate all 12 student groups for their exceptional work in reimagining architecture with empathy, resilience, and innovation.

title: Seu Architecture Student Represents Bangladesh At Aca21 In South Korea
clean_text: Jannatul Ferdous Megha, a student of the Department of Architecture, Southeast University, proudly represented Bangladesh at the 21st Asian Congress of Architects (ACA21), at Incheon Songdo Convensia & Incheon area, South Korea. Hosted by KIRA in collaboration with Incheon Metropolitan City, this prestigious congress gathered approximately 20,000 domestic and international architects, industry professionals, and the general public. The program featured major events including the Opening Ceremony, Keynote Speech, Special Lecture, Keynote Forum, ARCASIA Council Meeting & Subcommittee sessions, Architect's Night, Public Program, and Friendship Night. Under the overarching theme of "A Better Tomorrow," architects from across Asia came together to share knowledge, exchange ideas, and collectively envision a sustainable and forward-looking built environment.

title: Seu Architecture Department Hosts Lecture At Jury Space
clean_text: SEU Architecture Department Hosts Lecture at Jury Space The Department of Architecture along with Architecture Club, Southeast University organized a lecture at the Jury Space of the department as part of its regular lecture series. The session titled "Re-envisioning Andarkilla Shahi Jame Mosque" was conducted by Ar. Sabrina Aftab and Ar. Sadequl Bashar. Both speakers shared their insights and perspectives on rethinking the architectural and cultural significance of the historic mosque. The program began with a welcome address by Latifa Sultana, Assistant Professor, Department of Architecture, Southeast University. It was a dialogue-oriented session that encouraged interactive discussion among students and faculty members, enriching their understanding of architectural conservation and reinterpretation. The event was attended by faculty members and students of the department, making it a memorable and engaging academic exchange.

title: Rafiq Azam Travel Bursary
clean_text: The jury for the Rafiq Azam Travel Bursary (RATB) took place at the Department of Architecture, Southeast University. Six shortlisted participants presented their entries, and fourth-year student Sadman Hossain Rakin was selected as the grant recipient. The RATB program, established in 2010 by the award-winning architectural firm SHATOTTO Architecture for Green Living, offers a one-week solo residential work experience in one of seven listed countries, with all expenses covered. The jury board included Dr. Masud Ur Rashid (Chairman, Department of Architecture), Ar. Zannat Jui (Head of Design, SHATOTTO), Ar. Syed Monirul Islam (Associate Professor, SEU), Ar. Asijit Khan (Assistant Professor, WCFA, India), and Ar. Jubaida Gulshan Ara (Assistant Professor, SEU).

title: Faculty Members Present Research At International Conference Academic
clean_text: Several esteemed faculty members from the Department of Economics at Southeast University presented a research article titled "The Impact of Informal Multiple Borrowing on Fish Farmers' Economic Status: A Case Study of Rural Bangladesh" at the 6th NSRIC International Conference on Sustainable Education, Liberal Arts and Social Sciences. The research team included Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman of the Department of Economics; Ms. Fahima Kabir, Md. Hasan Mehedi, Md. Ashikur Rahman, Mohammad Asrarul Hasanat, and Ms. Sanjida Nourin. Their paper critically examines the financial challenges faced by rural fish farmers in Bangladesh due to informal multiple borrowing practices and highlights its broader economic implications. The presentation received positive feedback from participants for its relevance to sustainable rural development and inclusive financial practices. The Department congratulates the team for their valuable contribution and for representing Southeast University on an international academic platform.

Mofazzal Hossain, Pro Vice Chancellor, SEU; Prof. Dr. Farhana Helal Mehtab, Dean, SASS; Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman, Dept. of Economics; faculty members; and professionals from iSocial & CCDB participated.

title: Study Tour At Bangladesh Agricultural University Successfully Completed
clean_text: The Department of Economics at Southeast University successfully organized a study tour at Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU), Mymensingh, offering an insightful and engaging experience for students. The tour aimed to bridge theoretical knowledge with practical field experience in agricultural practices and economics. A group of enthusiastic students, accompanied by faculty members Ms. Ruba Rummana, Dr. Wasim Akram, and Md. Mominul Islam, participated in this educational excursion. The primary objective was to deepen students' understanding of the practical applications of Agricultural Economics and familiarize them with contemporary agricultural challenges and innovations. The students had the opportunity to interact with field experts and gain first-hand knowledge of modern farming techniques, crop management, and sustainable agricultural practices. Engaging discussions highlighted the importance of technology in enhancing productivity and addressing economic constraints in the agricultural sector. The study tour reflects the department's dedication to fostering an integrated education and practical learning opportunities for students.

title: Eco-Fest 2024-25: Journey Together, Thrive Forever
clean_text:
Eco-Fest 2024-25: Journey Together, Thrive Forever

Southeast University's Department of Economics hosted the vibrant Eco-Fest 2024-25, themed "Journey Together, Thrive Forever". The event highlighted the collective spirit of academic excellence, sustainable growth, and community development, engaging students, faculty, and alumni in a celebration of economics and sustainability. The festivities commenced with the inauguration by the Chief Guest, Prof. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam PhD, Vice Chancellor, Southeast University. The opening segment included a visit to vibrant stalls, showcasing student initiatives and projects, followed by a tree plantation drive symbolizing the department's commitment to sustainability. The academic session was formally initiated with a warm welcome speech by Dr. Kazi Tanvir Mahmud, Chairman of the Department of Economics. He reflected on the department's commitment to fostering intellectual growth and innovation. The core discussions delved deep into economic perspectives and global relevance. Special Guest Prof. Dr. Mohammed Helal Uddin from the University of Dhaka presented a thought-provoking analysis on "The Impact of the July Revolution on the Economy of Bangladesh". Prof. Dr. Md. Abdul Hakim, from Southeast University, offered insights into the nuanced concept of "Meaning of Development". The session's highlight was the inspirational speech by Prof. Dr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro Vice Chancellor Southeast University, followed by the address of the Chief Guest Prof. Yusuf Mahbubul Islam PhD, Vice Chancellor of the University. Both speakers emphasized the importance of collective effort and resilience in achieving progress and prosperity. The event concluded with a colorful cultural program, where students from the Department of Economics showcased their talents, marking a vibrant end to a memorable day.
